serviceIdentification.serviceDescription: TRM Labs provides blockchain intelligence and all-source AI investigation software that helps law enforcement, national security agencies, financial institutions, and cryptocurrency businesses detect, investigate, and disrupt fraud and financial crime. Delivered as multi-tenant Software as a Service from AWS GovCloud under the cloud service offering TRM Labs on GovCloud, the platform combines on-chain investigation with all-source intelligence. Investigators can trace cryptocurrency flows across over 66 blockchains and more than 1.9 billion assets in a single multi-chain graph with glass-box attribution, and resolve a lead - a name, an account, an address - across connected sources including corporate registries, sanctions data, and the dark web. All capabilities share a common identity and access management layer, workspace-based multi-tenancy, and a unified data plane within the GovCloud authorization boundary.

trustCenter.repositoryDescription: TRM's FedRAMP Trust Center — the complete and definitive source for FedRAMP Certification Data for TRM Labs on GovCloud, following the FedRAMP Certification Data Sharing rules.
trustCenter.accessRequestInstructions: Public FedRAMP service information and this machine-readable Certification Package Overview are available without authentication. Additional FedRAMP Certification Data is available to agency customers and other necessary parties by requesting access from the Trust Center landing page, which prompts for a work email address and routes the request to TRM for approval.

secureConfigurationGuidance.repositoryDescription: The TRM Labs GovCloud Secure Configuration Guide — secure configuration guidance for operating TRM Labs on GovCloud in the FedRAMP-recommended configuration in AWS GovCloud (us-gov-west-1). This URL is the guide's landing page; because the offering's products use different role models, it routes to a per-product edition for each. Each edition documents how to securely access, configure, operate, and decommission the top-level administrative account for a customer organization, the security-relevant settings only that account can operate and their security implications, the settings operable by privileged accounts, the recommended secure defaults, and the release history of those defaults.
secureConfigurationGuidance.accessRequestInstructions: Reading the guide on the TRM Labs Help Center (https://support.trmlabs.com) requires a sign-in. Any signed-in user of the product may read it: beyond the sign-in itself, no request, licence, non-disclosure agreement, or approval step applies, and TRM applies no per-requester sharing decision to this guide. TRM keeps the guide behind sign-in deliberately — it documents the administrative configuration of a commercial offering in operational detail, and every intended reader is a signed-in agency customer administrator. An agency that is evaluating the offering and does not yet hold an account, an assessor who needs to review the guide, or any reader who needs it in another format or pinned to a specific date for their own records, may request it from fedramp-security@trmlabs.com; TRM supplies it on request.

additionalRepositories.repositoryDescription: TRM Labs Documentation — product and developer documentation for the blockchain intelligence platform, including API reference and integration guides.
TRM Labs Help Center — task-based product guidance and release notes. Some individual articles require sign-in.

serviceProperties.documentationOverview: TRM supplies customer documentation across three properties. Product and developer documentation, including API reference and integration guides, is published openly at https://docs.trmlabs.com. Task-based product guidance and release notes are published in the TRM Labs Help Center at https://support.trmlabs.com, where some individual articles require sign-in. Security configuration guidance for operating the offering in its FedRAMP-recommended configuration is the Secure Configuration Guide, which is hosted in the Help Center and requires sign-in as an active, licensed TRM user; agency personnel and independent assessors without an account may request it at fedramp-security@trmlabs.com. Compliance artifacts, certifications, and FedRAMP Certification Data are shared through TRM's Trust Center at https://trust.trmlabs.com.

certifiedServices.serviceDescription: The certified offering is TRM Labs on GovCloud as a single bundle: blockchain intelligence and all-source AI investigation software, delivered as multi-tenant Software as a Service from AWS GovCloud and accessible through a secure web application and the TRM API. Its capabilities share one identity and access management layer, workspace-based multi-tenancy, and a unified data plane within the GovCloud authorization boundary.

certified.useCase: AWS GovCloud (US) — FedRAMP-authorized foundational IaaS (Rev5, High baseline; listed on the FedRAMP Marketplace as Class D (High), Agency path) per package F1603047866, hosting the entire TRM Labs on GovCloud trust boundary in us-gov-west-1; inherit IaaS/PaaS controls via the AWS Customer Responsibility Matrix. Inheritance is a claim TRM verifies against the AWS CRM, not a default.

serviceIdentification.serviceDescription:
Knox Systems provides a multi-tenant cloud platform for delivering commercial software to federal government customers. Customer applications deploy on Knox's managed infrastructure across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud Platform using Kubernetes containers, serverless functions, or virtual machines. Knox provides 24/7 Security Operations Center and Network Operations Center management, continuous security monitoring, vulnerability scanning, patch management, and incident response for all customer workloads. This includes:

Adobe Connect is designed for immersive synchronous online meeting experiences for training, large-scale webinars, and virtual classroom meetings for a distributed workforce.

Adobe Learning Manager (ALM) is an asynchronous Learning Management System that enables Learning and Development teams to drive personalized learning experiences across multiple devices.

Class Technologies Inc. (class.com) is the next generation virtual learning environment that enables active learning, collaboration, and engagement in online classes and virtual instructor-led training.

Spacelift delivers a FedRAMP-compliant IaC automation platform for secure and efficient cloud infrastructure management. It streamlines OpenTofu, Terraform, Pulumi, and Kubernetes workflows with robust policy enforcement and secret management for government agencies.

Tovuti LMS and Tovuti Waypoints: Best of Class Compliance Training and AI Course Authoring in Minutes not Months - Tovuti LMS is a FedRAMP Moderate authorized platform built for federal agencies, delivering secure learner management, automated compliance tracking, role-based access controls, and real-time reporting across your workforce. For AI course authoring, Tovuti Waypoints converts your agency's source materials into interactive, Section 508-compliant SCORM courses. Instantly transform policy PDFs and procedures into ready-to-deploy training, accelerating your response to new mandates with a platform built for both speed and security.

Celonis Process Mining (CPM4) is the world's leading data-driven process optimization platform that helps organizations automatically discover inefficiencies, ensure compliance, and identify improvement opportunities across business processes through real-time analytics and visualization.

Backupta is a Resilience Platform for Okta that ensures uninterrupted identity and access management. It delivers secure backup, disaster recovery, and rapid restoration of tenants or objects. Tenant cloning and failover strengthen business continuity, while proactive monitoring and audit logs enhance security.

Kovr.AI accelerates compliance authorizations (FedRAMP, CMMC, DOD SRG) from months to minutes by automating gap assessments and ATO package generation, instantly identifying compliant controls and remediation needs, then auto-generating required authorization documentation including SSPs, POA&Ms, and policies. The platform connects to environments via read-only integrations—or accepts direct evidence uploads—enabling teams to rapidly and continuously monitor and assess their security configurations, logs, policies, evidence, and artifacts using state-of-the-art Large Language Models (LLMs).

OutSystems enables federal agencies to rapidly build, manage, and scale mission-critical digital solutions with government-grade security, reliability, and governance built in. The platform supports the entire software development lifecycle, including integrated DevSecOps capabilities, enabling teams to deliver better frontline digital services and modernize core mission systems significantly faster. Agencies can accelerate delivery without extensive re-skilling, expanding development teams, or taking on the risks and costs associated with vendor lock-in.

Armis APEX Manage provides federal administrators a "single pane of glass" to aggregate operational data across multi-tenant Armis Centrix deployments. It eliminates manual per-tenant logins by centralizing health metrics and consolidated reporting into a unified oversight interface.

Resilinc Supply Chain Risk and Compliance Platform - Resilinc provides federal agencies with enterprise-level visibility and risk management across multi-tier supplier networks. The platform utilizes AI-driven workflows to automate disruption monitoring, forced labor compliance assessments (including UFLPA), and trade impact analysis. This SaaS solution streamlines oversight, allowing organizations to proactively identify and mitigate vulnerabilities within the global supply chain.

BigID provides an automated foundation for data security, privacy, and governance across the federal enterprise. The platform proactively discovers, architectures, and inventories sensitive data and AI assets across all environments—including multi-cloud, on-premises data centers, and data pipelines. By utilizing advanced machine learning for deep data classification, BigID enables agencies to automatically identify PII, PHI, and CUI. This visibility allows organizations to mitigate risk, enforce granular access controls, and ensure regulatory compliance. From automating data lifecycle management to securing the data fed into AI models, BigID transforms fragmented information into a secure, searchable, and compliant asset.

Procurement Sciences offers a secure, end-to-end AI platform purpose-built for government contractors to find, qualify, manage, and win federal and SLED opportunities. The Awarded AI platform uses advanced generative and agentic AI to identify and surface relevant opportunities, evaluate bid/no-bid fit, manage capture and pipeline activities, extract and shred requirements, generate structured proposal outlines and first drafts, and automate compliance review and quality checks prior to submission. With human-in-the-loop oversight embedded across AI-powered workflows, the platform accelerates response timelines, strengthens compliance accuracy, improves proposal quality, and drives revenue growth without compromising security.

Presage Technologies delivers a contactless physiological and behavioral assessment platform leveraging advanced video-based capture and analysis across in-person and fully remote environments. The platform identifies physiological signals and micromovements from video input, surfacing actionable response patterns and real-time indicators through an intuitive interface that empowers expert analysts to observe, annotate, and interpret findings with speed and confidence. Purpose-built for federal agencies and authorized mission partners, the system supports a broad range of high-value use cases and decision-making workflows requiring non-contact assessment at scale.

Brightfin is a ServiceNow-native telecom and IT financial management application that consolidates enterprise wireless, wireline, and cloud spend into a single platform for invoice processing, cost allocation, asset lifecycle management, and carrier integrations. Brightfin provides finance, IT, and procurement teams with authoritative control over telecom and technology costs directly within their ServiceNow environment.

Serval is an AI-native enterprise service management platform that automates employee requests, onboarding/offboarding, just-in-time access, and more. Serval allows IT, Security, HR, and other functions to eliminate repetitive work with AI agents while maintaining enterprise-grade security and governance.

GovEagle is a purpose-built software-as-a-service (SaaS) platform that helps U.S. government contractors plan, analyze, draft, and manage responses to federal solicitations, addressing the mission need for faster, higher-quality, and more compliant proposal development. The authorization boundary is a multi-tenant SaaS application hosted in AWS GovCloud (US) with logical isolation between customer tenants, used by contractors' business development, capture, and proposal teams to process business and proposal data that may include Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI).

Fieldguide is an AI-native platform transforming how audit, advisory, and assurance work gets done. Purpose-built for regulated environments, Fieldguide brings professionals and agentic AI together to modernize engagement delivery from planning through close, enabling audit and advisory practitioners to deliver higher-quality work, strengthen client experiences, and unlock growth for the decade ahead.

ThreatModeler Nexus is a threat modeling platform that ingests architecture artifacts, source code, infrastructure-as-code, and system documentation to build and maintain models of an organization's applications and infrastructure, identify security threats and required controls, and generate audit-ready reports; it exists to give organizations a continuously updated, centralized record of system security design rather than relying on manual, point-in-time assessments. Within the authorization boundary, the system covers the model-building, analysis, and reporting components that process customer-submitted architecture and code artifacts and produce the resulting threat/control/compliance data; it is delivered as a single, dedicated-tenant SaaS application meaning each customer has its own isolated instance with system mapping, graph management, and reporting functioning as the major internal components. Users include security architects, developers, and security/compliance leaders at customer organizations, who submit system data (architecture diagrams, code, infrastructure configurations, and related business/technical metadata not typically PII beyond user account information) and consume the resulting risk and compliance outputs; the system depends on customer-provided source repositories and documentation as external inputs to build its models.

AidFinder is a Software as a Service (SaaS) platform that helps disaster survivors identify, apply for, and track federal and state emergency assistance programs, primarily FEMA Individual Assistance. The system supports both preparedness and disaster response workflows: before a disaster, it analyzes property-level insurance coverage gaps across six hazard categories — flood, fire, wind, earthquake, snow/ice, and volcano — to help users understand their financial exposure relative to rebuild cost; after a disaster declaration, it evaluates survivor household profiles against program-specific eligibility rules using factors including property ownership, occupancy status, damage severity, insurance coverage, household composition, and income, then orchestrates AI-driven agents that automate end-to-end application submission on the survivor's behalf directly on DisasterAssistance.gov. The platform is delivered as a cloud-native, multi-tenant SaaS application used by disaster survivors and program administrators, and processes Tier 1/2 PII including names, addresses, Social Security data, financial records, property records, and damage documentation. Key external dependencies include FEMA's DisasterAssistance.gov for application submission, Socure for identity verification, Plaid for bank account linking, Mapbox for geospatial disaster visualization.

Solve Intelligence is a single-tenant SaaS system for authorized examiners, attorneys, technical specialists, reviewers, supervisors, and administrators who perform government patent work. The system supports examination, legal analysis, document review, research, and drafting, and processes patent records, prior art, business data, CUI, and PII. The authorization boundary contains the web application, workflow, AI, search, and storage services, with dependencies on cloud hosting, identity services, and approved information sources.

Sweetspot is a cloud-based, multi-tenant AI platform that enables federal agencies, government contractors, and enterprises to configure, run, and manage complex workflows using their data, institutional knowledge, people, and connected systems. For government contractors, Sweetspot automates work across the business development and bid lifecycle, including opportunity discovery, federal market research, teaming, pipeline and capture management, compliance and capability matrix development, and proposal drafting, with configurable human review and approval steps. Native Microsoft 365 integrations support workflow execution and collaboration across Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, Word, PowerPoint, and Excel.

The platform operates within a single FedRAMP 20x Class C certification boundary with a unified continuous-monitoring and automated evidence program. trustCenter.repositoryDescription: Specset Trust Center, the single repository for FedRAMP Certification Data for the Specset Cloud Platform. The landing page, compliance posture summary, subprocessor list and FedRAMP milestone information are public. The SOC 2 Type II report is published there as a restricted resource today. The remaining Class A certification data — the Security Decision Record, the example Ongoing Certification Report, the information-resources inventory with its generator and sources, the Incident Response Procedure, the Vulnerability Management Procedure, the security policies maintained in Vanta, and twelve supporting-evidence documents, one per artifact the Security Decision Record cites — is supplied with the Class A application and published here as restricted resources when that application is filed. The Security Decision Record, the example Ongoing Certification Report and the inventory are published in both machine-readable and human-readable form. Gap: only the SOC 2 Type II report is open to access requests today. Plan: publish the rest as restricted resources, byte-identical to the filed package, when the Class A application is filed.
trustCenter.accessRequestInstructions: The landing page at https://trust.specset.com requires no login. FedRAMP staff and agency reviewers request access to the restricted FedRAMP Certification Data from the Trust Center page. certifiedServices.serviceDescription: The Specset Cloud Platform is a single multi-tenant SaaS service for construction document intelligence. Security category: Moderate (FIPS 199), reflecting the Controlled Unclassified Information the service handles for defense and federal customers. The platform is offered as a single service, and no component of it carries a different security category. It ingests customer project documents (project manuals and specifications, drawing sheets, shop drawings and submittals) and provides automated submittal review against project specifications, UFGS and specification compliance checking, design review automation, document search and question answering across a project's documents, and asset management logic. Customers use the service through a web application. Optional customer-initiated integrations connect to the customer's own Procore or Autodesk tenants. Production runs on Google Cloud Platform in project specset-prod-assured (Assured Workloads, FEDRAMP_MODERATE control package, us-west1), with supporting services on Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure as listed under third-party information resources. A per-organization CUI mode restricts model, embedding and web-grounding calls to the Assured Workloads project (Vertex AI, location us), disables the commercial AI and support-chat integrations and the customer-initiated Procore and Autodesk integrations, and never calls Perplexity. Federal tenants are provisioned with CUI mode enabled.

certified.useCase: Google Cloud Platform (Google Services) — primary hosting of all production infrastructure in project specset-prod-assured (Assured Workloads): GKE Autopilot, Cloud SQL, Cloud Storage, Memorystore, Cloud KMS, Cloud Load Balancing and Cloud Armor, Cloud Logging and Monitoring, Secret Manager, Artifact Registry, and Vertex AI (Gemini) model inference, embeddings and Web Grounding for Enterprise. Organizations in CUI mode use Vertex AI in the Assured Workloads project at location us only; other organizations use Vertex AI in a peer Google Cloud project, specbook-production, outside Assured Workloads. Stores and processes customer data. A third Google Cloud project, specbook-development, holds the development user-content buckets, development service identity and development vendor-key secrets; it sits outside Assured Workloads and inside the assessment scope because it shares integration credentials and software delivery with production. A founder-run project-clone tool can copy a production project's documents into that development environment for debugging, so development stores may hold customer content. Two further Google Cloud projects are inside the assessment scope and hold no customer content: specset-dataroom, an investor data room with no connection to the offering, and vanta-scanner, which holds the compliance scanner's federated identity and read-only custom roles outside the boundary project. Gap: the clone tool does not yet exclude the projects of organizations in CUI mode. Plan: block cloning of CUI-mode organizations in the tool and record the rule in the production-access procedure before the 2026-12-01 Ongoing Certification Report.

AWS US East/West — supporting services: Amazon SES (transactional email), Route 53 (DNS), S3 (CI build cache, CloudTrail audit logs, and a legacy database-backup bucket from the pre-2026 hosting platform), GuardDuty (threat detection), and Amazon Bedrock (Claude model inference in us-west-2, for organizations not in CUI mode; prompts may include customer document text).

Azure Commercial Cloud — Azure OpenAI (GPT model inference for organizations not in CUI mode; prompts may include customer document text) and Microsoft Entra ID application registrations for customer 'Sign in with Microsoft' single sign-on. No customer data is stored on Azure.

Google Workspace — provider identity (Cloud Identity) for staff access to production through Identity-Aware Proxy, with security-key or passkey 2-Step Verification enforced for all staff; staff email including the FedRAMP Security Inbox. No customer data.

GitHub Enterprise Cloud — source control and CI/CD for the application and infrastructure-as-code. Dependabot security alerts and CodeQL code scanning run on the application and infrastructure repositories, with Dependabot version updates on the infrastructure repository. Deploys to production through OpenID Connect workload identity federation. No customer data.

Vanta Trust Management Platform — continuous configuration monitoring of the production cloud accounts (read-only metadata), compliance evidence and policies, and the Specset Trust Center at trust.specset.com. No customer data.
Slack — operational alerting and change-notification channel for the provider (infrastructure change notifications, security alerts). Resource metadata only; no customer data.

Perplexity Enterprise and API Platform (FedRAMP Certified, Class B) — web search for AI features of organizations not in CUI mode. Receives model-generated search queries; customer documents are not sent. Never called for organizations in CUI mode: their web lookups run on Vertex AI Web Grounding for Enterprise inside the Google Cloud Assured Workloads project.

Prompts may include customer document text, and inference runs in Cloudflare data centers worldwide. Cloudflare also supplies the edge fronting for the Trust Center custom hostname (trust.specset.com) as part of Vanta's Trust Center service; that use carries no customer data. nonCertified.provider: Apryse Software Inc. (formerly PDFTron Systems Inc.)
nonCertified.useCase: Document-processing software from one vendor, used two ways, both inside the boundary or in the user's browser. The server-side PDF library runs in the application and worker pods on customer documents, and the structured-output module it needs is downloaded from the vendor at container image build and pinned by SHA-256 checksum. The browser viewer runs under an offline OEM license key, so viewing makes no call to the vendor. No customer document data is sent to the vendor; the resource is in scope as a software-supply-chain dependency that affects document-processing availability and build integrity.

nonCertified.name: Autodesk Platform Services
nonCertified.useCase: Optional customer-initiated integration to the customer's own Autodesk tenant through OAuth; the customer chooses and authorizes the data exchanged. nonCertified.name: Procore

Plan: deploy the gate before the paid federal pilot.

nonCertified.name: Claude Code (Anthropic) — engineering assistant
nonCertified.useCase: Coding assistant used by the founders on operator laptops. It is in the assessment scope because what it reads can include federal customer data: production configuration, cluster state, metadata and application logs read as a dedicated read-only service account, and database rows read through a time-limited tunnel that a founder approves each session. What it reads is sent to the model provider. The service account holds reader roles only and has no write permission on production. Database reads use Cloud SQL IAM authentication with SELECT-only grants. Every tunnel start is recorded as an Admin Activity audit entry, and an alert fires if the account ever appears as the principal of a write. Gap: rows of organizations in CUI mode are not yet excluded from that read-only database role. Plan: enforce the exclusion with row-level security before the 2026-12-01 Ongoing Certification Report.

nonCertified.name: OpenAI Codex — engineering assistant
nonCertified.useCase: Coding assistant used by the founders on operator laptops. It is in the assessment scope under the same production-access protocol as Claude Code. It reads as the dedicated read-only service account with no write permission on production, and reads database rows only through the founder-approved, SELECT-only, time-limited tunnel. Every tunnel start is recorded as an Admin Activity audit entry, and an alert fires on any write. What it reads is sent to the model provider. The same planned exclusion of CUI-mode rows applies.

nonCertified.name: Firecrawl
nonCertified.useCase: Two dependencies on one vendor. The hosted scraper reads public bid-portal pages for specification research and receives the page URL together with the extraction instructions the assistant's model wrote, which may derive from a user's conversation; no document, embedding or database row is sent. The vendor's PDF parser is a pinned software dependency that runs inside the boundary on customer PDFs, so no customer document reaches the vendor through it. Gap: the scrape tool is not gated on CUI mode, so an organization in CUI mode can reach this non-certified vendor. Plan: apply the integration CUI gate to the tool and its workflow activity before the 2026-12-01 Ongoing Certification Report.

nonCertified.name: CARTO basemaps
nonCertified.useCase: Browser-side raster map tiles for one dashboard panel, the closeout facility map. The vendor receives the visitor's IP address and the requested tile coordinates, which disclose the approximate location of a project facility; no project name, address, identifier or document is sent, and no server-side path to the vendor exists. Gap: those tile requests are not gated on CUI mode. Plan: self-host the tiles and remove the egress before the 2026-12-01 Ongoing Certification Report.

nonCertified.name: Customer single sign-on identity providers (Google Sign-In and customer-configured OpenID Connect providers)
nonCertified.provider: The customer's own identity provider (Google Sign-In, or any OpenID Connect provider a customer configures)
nonCertified.useCase: Customer-chosen authentication for customer users. Specset receives the identity assertion and the claims the customer's provider releases; no project document or row leaves the boundary. Each provider is the customer's own information resource under the customer's own administration, so its certification status is the customer's decision. serviceIdentification.serviceDescription:
GCS is a FedRAMP Moderate (previously JAB P-ATO authorized) IaaS/PaaS/SaaS platform offering scalable compute, private cloud, and SaaS solutions to federal agencies. Customers may deploy on shared infrastructure, provision a dedicated private cloud, or co-locate their own hardware within the GCS authorization boundary.

Overview of Authorized Services

Compute (IaaS)
Configurable virtual machines balancing CPU, RAM, and high-I/O flash storage; available as pre-hardened images or custom builds.

Private FedRAMP Cloud (IaaS)
Dedicated, tenant-isolated compute, networking, and storage fully within the GCS boundary for agencies requiring resource segregation.

Bring Your Own Hardware
Customer-owned hardware co-located within the GCS boundary, leveraging inherited GCS controls for specialized appliances and equipment.

Virtual Desktop Services (DaaS)
Browser-accessible virtual desktops hosted within the GCS boundary, providing agency users with secure, managed access to applications and data from any endpoint without local installation requirements.

Authorization as a Service (AaaS)
Enables SaaS providers to inherit GCS controls and deliver FedRAMP-authorized products under the GCS P-ATO.

Calabrio Workforce Engagement Management (SaaS)
Contact center workforce optimization suite covering scheduling, agent performance analytics, and business intelligence.

Sharetru Federal (SaaS)
Managed File Transfer as a Service (MFTaaS) supporting CMMC, ITAR, HIPAA, and PCI-DSS regulated data exchange.

Sayari Risk Intelligence (SaaS)
Supply chain and counterparty risk platform aggregating corporate ownership and trade data from 250+ jurisdictions.

GRID20/20 ATI (SaaS/IoT)
Cloud-based distribution grid and environmental monitoring platform covering wildfire detection, auto-alerting, and AI-enhanced analytics. Field sensor devices operate outside the authorization boundary and feed data into the GCS-hosted ATI application, which is fully within scope.

IGS Bridge (SaaS)
Secure, platform-agnostic integration suite connecting enterprise and legacy systems (Bridge Connect), coordinating clinical decision support (Bridge Care), standardizing data relationships (Bridge Map), and delivering real-time operational analytics (Bridge Monitor).

Automated Background Investigation System (ABIS)
ABIS is a personnel security case management system that tracks background investigations for Federal Employees, Contractors, Volunteers, and Interns from initiation through final adjudication. The system allows cases to be checked for transfer of trust, eApp initiation, and to conduct all pre-hire checks, and to make pre-hire and final adjudication determinations. The system also processes security clearances, SEAD-3 self-reporting, Detailee cases, and other types of cases. Interfaces with DCSA's eDelivery, CVS, OF79a Adjudications, and other interfaces are included in the system. The system fully implements Continuous Vetting (CV) and RapBack enrollment/unenrollment and processing of alerts received from CV/Rapback

NXXUS Unified Imaging Intelligence Platform
NXXUS is a federated enterprise imaging, clinical data, workflow, and AI orchestration platform. With NXXUS, healthcare organizations no longer need to replace their existing infrastructure or undertake a massive data migration; NXXUS creates a unified access and intelligence layer across those systems.

certifiedServices.serviceDescription: The Specset Cloud Platform is a single multi-tenant SaaS service for construction document intelligence. Security category: Moderate (FIPS 199), reflecting the Controlled Unclassified Information the service handles for defense and federal customers. The platform is offered as a single service, and no component of it carries a different security category. It ingests customer project documents (project manuals and specifications, drawing sheets, shop drawings and submittals) and provides automated submittal review against project specifications, UFGS and specification compliance checking, design review automation, document search and question answering across a project's documents, and asset management logic. Customers use the service through a web application. Optional customer-initiated integrations connect to the customer's own Procore or Autodesk tenants. Production runs on Google Cloud Platform in project specset-prod-assured (Assured Workloads, FEDRAMP_MODERATE control package, us-west1), with supporting services on Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure as listed under third-party information resources. A per-organization CUI mode restricts model, embedding and web-grounding calls to the Assured Workloads project (Vertex AI, location us), disables the commercial AI and support-chat integrations and the customer-initiated Procore and Autodesk integrations, and never calls Perplexity. Federal tenants are provisioned with CUI mode enabled.

certified.useCase: Google Cloud Platform (Google Services) — primary hosting of all production infrastructure in project specset-prod-assured (Assured Workloads): GKE Autopilot, Cloud SQL, Cloud Storage, Memorystore, Cloud KMS, Cloud Load Balancing and Cloud Armor, Cloud Logging and Monitoring, Secret Manager, Artifact Registry, and Vertex AI (Gemini) model inference, embeddings and Web Grounding for Enterprise. Organizations in CUI mode use Vertex AI in the Assured Workloads project at location us only; other organizations use Vertex AI in a peer Google Cloud project, specbook-production, outside Assured Workloads. Stores and processes customer data. A third Google Cloud project, specbook-development, holds the development user-content buckets, development service identity and development vendor-key secrets; it sits outside Assured Workloads and inside the assessment scope because it shares integration credentials and software delivery with production. A founder-run project-clone tool can copy a production project's documents into that development environment for debugging, so development stores may hold customer content. Two further Google Cloud projects are inside the assessment scope and hold no customer content: specset-dataroom, an investor data room with no connection to the offering, and vanta-scanner, which holds the compliance scanner's federated identity and read-only custom roles outside the boundary project. Gap: the clone tool does not yet exclude the projects of organizations in CUI mode. Plan: block cloning of CUI-mode organizations in the tool and record the rule in the production-access procedure before the 2026-12-01 Ongoing Certification Report.

AWS US East/West — supporting services: Amazon SES (transactional email), Route 53 (DNS), S3 (CI build cache, CloudTrail audit logs, and a legacy database-backup bucket from the pre-2026 hosting platform), GuardDuty (threat detection), and Amazon Bedrock (Claude model inference in us-west-2, for organizations not in CUI mode; prompts may include customer document text).

Azure Commercial Cloud — Azure OpenAI (GPT model inference for organizations not in CUI mode; prompts may include customer document text) and Microsoft Entra ID application registrations for customer 'Sign in with Microsoft' single sign-on. No customer data is stored on Azure.

Google Workspace — provider identity (Cloud Identity) for staff access to production through Identity-Aware Proxy, with security-key or passkey 2-Step Verification enforced for all staff; staff email including the FedRAMP Security Inbox. No customer data.

GitHub Enterprise Cloud — source control and CI/CD for the application and infrastructure-as-code. Dependabot security alerts and CodeQL code scanning run on the application and infrastructure repositories, with Dependabot version updates on the infrastructure repository. Deploys to production through OpenID Connect workload identity federation. No customer data.

Vanta Trust Management Platform — continuous configuration monitoring of the production cloud accounts (read-only metadata), compliance evidence and policies, and the Specset Trust Center at trust.specset.com. No customer data.
Slack — operational alerting and change-notification channel for the provider (infrastructure change notifications, security alerts). Resource metadata only; no customer data.

Perplexity Enterprise and API Platform (FedRAMP Certified, Class B) — web search for AI features of organizations not in CUI mode. Receives model-generated search queries; customer documents are not sent. Never called for organizations in CUI mode: their web lookups run on Vertex AI Web Grounding for Enterprise inside the Google Cloud Assured Workloads project.

nonCertified.name: Anthropic API (Claude, direct)
nonCertified.useCase: Direct Claude model inference for a small set of models not served through Amazon Bedrock, selectable only by Specset administrators; prompts may include customer document text. Never enabled for organizations in CUI mode.

nonCertified.name: Intercom
nonCertified.useCase: In-app customer support chat for organizations not in CUI mode. Processes customer user contact details and support conversation content; no project documents. The messenger never loads for an organization in CUI mode and its memberships are never shared with Intercom.

nonCertified.name: Google Generative AI (AI Studio)
nonCertified.useCase: Gemini API path outside the Google Cloud FedRAMP boundary, used as the embedding provider for organizations not in CUI mode; prompts may include customer document text. Never used for organizations in CUI mode, whose embeddings run on Vertex AI in the Assured Workloads project. Retirement is planned before the Class C application.

nonCertified.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
nonCertified.useCase: Cloudflare AI Gateway and Workers AI for experimental open-model inference selectable by organizations not in CUI mode. Prompts may include customer document text, and inference runs in Cloudflare data centers worldwide. The gateway does not store prompt or completion payloads, and the per-organization CUI mode excludes it. Cloudflare also supplies the edge fronting for the Trust Center custom hostname (trust.specset.com) as part of Vanta's Trust Center service; that use carries no customer data. The Cloudflare for Government offering is not used.

nonCertified.name: NOAA / National Weather Service APIs
nonCertified.provider: US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (federal agency)
nonCertified.useCase: Public weather and tide data for project daily logs. Receives a project site's latitude and longitude only; forecasts and tide data are returned to the daily log. Nothing is stored at the service. A US federal government data service, not a cloud service offering.

nonCertified.name: Apryse
nonCertified.provider: Apryse Software Inc. (formerly PDFTron Systems Inc.)
nonCertified.useCase: Document-processing software from one vendor, used two ways, both inside the boundary or in the user's browser. The server-side PDF library runs in the application and worker pods on customer documents, and the structured-output module it needs is downloaded from the vendor at container image build and pinned by SHA-256 checksum. The browser viewer runs under an offline OEM license key, so viewing makes no call to the vendor. No customer document data is sent to the vendor; the resource is in scope as a software-supply-chain dependency that affects document-processing availability and build integrity.

nonCertified.name: Autodesk Platform Services
nonCertified.useCase: Optional customer-initiated integration to the customer's own Autodesk tenant through OAuth; the customer chooses and authorizes the data exchanged. Disabled for organizations in CUI mode. Not used unless a customer connects it. Gap: the application gate that stops an organization in CUI mode from connecting the integration, and makes an existing connection inert, is written and reviewed but not yet deployed, so CUI mode does not disable this integration today. Plan: deploy the gate before the paid federal pilot.

nonCertified.name: Procore
nonCertified.useCase: Optional customer-initiated integration to the customer's own Procore tenant through OAuth; the customer chooses and authorizes the data exchanged. Disabled for organizations in CUI mode. Not used unless a customer connects it. Gap: the application gate that stops an organization in CUI mode from connecting the integration, and makes an existing connection inert, is written and reviewed but not yet deployed, so CUI mode does not disable this integration today. Plan: deploy the gate before the paid federal pilot.

nonCertified.name: Claude Code (Anthropic) — engineering assistant
nonCertified.useCase: Coding assistant used by the founders on operator laptops. It is in the assessment scope because what it reads can include federal customer data: production configuration, cluster state, metadata and application logs read as a dedicated read-only service account, and database rows read through a time-limited tunnel that a founder approves each session. What it reads is sent to the model provider. The service account holds reader roles only and has no write permission on production. Database reads use Cloud SQL IAM authentication with SELECT-only grants. Every tunnel start is recorded as an Admin Activity audit entry, and an alert fires if the account ever appears as the principal of a write. Gap: rows of organizations in CUI mode are not yet excluded from that read-only database role. Plan: enforce the exclusion with row-level security before the 2026-12-01 Ongoing Certification Report.

nonCertified.name: OpenAI Codex — engineering assistant
nonCertified.useCase: Coding assistant used by the founders on operator laptops. It is in the assessment scope under the same production-access protocol as Claude Code. It reads as the dedicated read-only service account with no write permission on production, and reads database rows only through the founder-approved, SELECT-only, time-limited tunnel. Every tunnel start is recorded as an Admin Activity audit entry, and an alert fires on any write. What it reads is sent to the model provider. The same planned exclusion of CUI-mode rows applies.

nonCertified.name: Firecrawl
nonCertified.useCase: Two dependencies on one vendor. The hosted scraper reads public bid-portal pages for specification research and receives the page URL together with the extraction instructions the assistant's model wrote, which may derive from a user's conversation; no document, embedding or database row is sent. The vendor's PDF parser is a pinned software dependency that runs inside the boundary on customer PDFs, so no customer document reaches the vendor through it. Gap: the scrape tool is not gated on CUI mode, so an organization in CUI mode can reach this non-certified vendor. Plan: apply the integration CUI gate to the tool and its workflow activity before the 2026-12-01 Ongoing Certification Report.

nonCertified.name: CARTO basemaps
nonCertified.useCase: Browser-side raster map tiles for one dashboard panel, the closeout facility map. The vendor receives the visitor's IP address and the requested tile coordinates, which disclose the approximate location of a project facility; no project name, address, identifier or document is sent, and no server-side path to the vendor exists. Gap: those tile requests are not gated on CUI mode. Plan: self-host the tiles and remove the egress before the 2026-12-01 Ongoing Certification Report.

nonCertified.name: Customer single sign-on identity providers (Google Sign-In and customer-configured OpenID Connect providers)
nonCertified.provider: The customer's own identity provider (Google Sign-In, or any OpenID Connect provider a customer configures)
nonCertified.useCase: Customer-chosen authentication for customer users. Specset receives the identity assertion and the claims the customer's provider releases; no project document or row leaves the boundary. Each provider is the customer's own information resource under the customer's own administration, so its certification status is the customer's decision. Corporate Google single sign-on is enforced for Specset staff and superadmin access.

serviceIdentification.serviceDescription:
The GSSOne AWS is a General Support System (GSS) operated by Project Hosts and deployed within AWS GovCloud. The platform is designed as a secure, multi-tenant PaaS/SaaS environment that enables federal, DoD, state, local, and tribal agencies, as well as government contractors, members of the DIB and the public to deploy and operate applications in compliance with federal security requirements.

The GSSOne AWS Core provides a standardized set of centrally managed services that support secure application deployment and operations, including: access control, authentication, auditing, monitoring, scanning, patching, configuration management, malware prevention, intrusion prevention, incident response, backup, and disaster recovery.

These capabilities are implemented and managed by Project Hosts and are leveraged by applications deployed on the platform to meet security and compliance requirements.

GSSOne AWS supports two primary application deployment models:

**1. Applications Included Within the GSS One Authorization Boundary**

Certain SaaS applications are incorporated directly into the GSSOne AWS authorization boundary and are assessed and certified as part of the GSSOne AWS system.

**2. Applications Supported on the Platform**

GSSOne AWS also supports customer and Independent Software Vendor (ISV) applications that are deployed on the platform but maintain their own authorization boundary (e.g., agency ATO or ISV-owned system).

In this model, Project Hosts provides the underlying infrastructure, security services, and operational support, while the application owner maintains responsibility for their system authorization and application-specific controls.

This flexible deployment model allows agencies to either leverage existing SaaS capabilities or deploy their own applications within a secure, FedRAMP-authorized environment.

**Applications Included Within the GSS One Authorization Boundary**

These applications are deployed, secured, and operated as part of the GSSOne AWS system and certification.

The following SaaS applications are currently included within the GSSOne AWS authorization boundary:

- **GSSOne AWS Portal/Admin Page**

Provided by Project Hosts this application provides user and administrative interfaces for account management, access provisioning, and operational support activities

- **JAMIS Prime ERP**

Provided and managed by JAMIS software, JAMIS Prime ERP is a platform that provides browser and mobile access to finance, project accounting, contract management, billing, and operational workflows for U.S. government contractors. The system supports core functions including job cost/project accounting, contract and subcontract management, budgeting and forecasting, general ledger, cash management, accounts receivable/payable, timecards, expense reporting, fixed assets, distribution management, and project manufacturing. JAMIS Prime streamlines contract management and billing by centralizing documents, automating workflows and approvals, tracking contract actions and funding, supporting government-compliant billing across common contract types, and managing revenue recognition, cost ceilings, retention, labor categories, markups, ACRN funding, and contract-specific billing rules. These capabilities help improve visibility, collaboration, invoice accuracy, and timely payment processing across the contract lifecycle.

- **Siemens Federal Cloud (SFC)**

Provided and Managed by Siemens Government Technology,The primary software application suite within SFC consists of the Teamcenter Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) software, which is a product and process digital thread management system.  Teamcenter PLM provides full product lifecycle data management services for a customer authored end item (to include requirements, product(s) and processes) and enables customer teams to better connect with each other on relevant data needed to make informed decisions throughout a product’s lifecycle.  Teamcenter offers integration capabilities with various CAD products, serving as the central hub for managing design data throughout the product lifecycle. Teamcenter ensures that all CAD models, assemblies, and drawings are securely stored, version-controlled, and accessible within the environment. This integration allows engineers to work directly within their preferred CAD authoring tools while benefiting from Teamcenter's data management, workflow automation, and collaboration features.

- **Perseus™**

Provided and managed by Chainbridge Solutions Inc., Perseus™ is a cloud-native SaaS product purpose-built to transform personnel security (PERSEC) workflows across the federal government. Blending deep PERSEC expertise with the scalability and performance of commercial software, Perseus™ streamlines clearance processes, enables Trusted Workforce readiness, and equips agencies with the clarity, efficiency, and confidence they need to deliver from day one.

- **FutureFeed and Cyber Illumination Application Environment (FutureFeed)**

Provided and managed by Continuous Compliance, There are two main components that make up the FutureFeed environment. FutureFeed is a robust, SaaS-based compliance management platform. Using FutureFeed’s powerful automation and reporting capabilities, organizations create a security-oriented culture that permeates the organization. Organizations use FutureFeed to create and maintain information security programs that comply with legal and regulatory requirements, and to prove compliance at any time.

Cyber Illumination is a supply chain communication, risk identification, and risk management tool. Federal agencies, government contractors, and commercial entities can use Cyber Illumination to gain better insight into and control over the risks, including cybersecurity risks, associated with their vendors and business partners. Clients can leverage Cyber Illumination’s built-in questionnaires, or create custom questionnaires, to gain the knowledge they need to better manage their supply chain risks. When a client’s vendor also uses FutureFeed, the vendor and the client enjoy seamless integration and robust, automated information sharing that takes the hassles out of supply chain risk management.

**Applications Supported on the Platform**

GSSOne AWS also supports customer and Independent Software Vendor (ISV) applications that are deployed on the platform but maintain their own authorization boundary (e.g., agency ATO or ISV-owned system). Each of the systems below have been vetted and meets the FedRAMP requirements and are ready to pursue FedRAMP certification or have been certified under their own listing and are viewable under the dependent product list.

Examples of supported applications include:

- 1Factory (1Factory)
- 202 Group/ BlueVoyant Government Services (Supply Chain Command)
- Brightly (Brightly Software)
- Caveonix (Caveonix Platform)
- CloudApper (Cloudapper.ai)
- H2O.ai (H2O.ai Cloud for Government)
- Invicti (Invicti AppSec Platform)
- Microsoft (Office, Dynamics, Power BI Server, Project Server, SharePoint, SSRS)
- ProSymmetry
- San Luis Aviation, Inc. (ESChat)
- TELCLOUD (TELCLOUD)
- TCP Software (TimeClock Plus)
- WordPress (WordPress CMS)
- WordPress As a Service (WPaaS)

For each of these applications, Project Hosts provides deployment, security, and operational support services for these applications, enabling customers to leverage the GSSOne AWS platform while maintaining flexibility in how their systems are authorized and managed. Performing these functions on the partner’s behalf allows the software vendors to focus on their core business model in delivering a secure, highly functional application to the agency while Project Hosts handles the security/ compliance requirements.

In either scenario, GSSOne AWS customers also are provided with access to the following systems running on the GSS One Azure system.

**GSS One Command Center (GSSOCC)**

The GSS One Command Center is a centralized compliance and operations platform that gives agencies and CSP partners real-time visibility into system security, risk, and authorization status. Designed to meet FedRAMP Rev. 5 BIRs and aligned with the direction of FedRAMP 20x, the GSSOCC supports a shift toward continuous, evidence-driven validation rather than static, point-in-time assessments.

It serves as a single pane of glass for managing the full lifecycle of authorization and operations, bringing together system documentation, vulnerability data, incident tracking, change control, and monitoring into one integrated experience. By linking controls directly to supporting evidence and operational data, the GSSOCC reduces the overhead of maintaining compliance and enables faster, more transparent ATO decisions for agencies.

**GSS One Support Center:**

Project Hosts has configured a customer-facing support portal for creating and managing support tickets powered by Atlassian Jira. This allows customers to view all of their relevant tickets, create tickets, submit change control requests, upload screenshots, review knowledgebases and communicate with PH staff through a secure channel.

serviceIdentification.serviceDescription: TrustGuard AI is a comprehensive, AI-native Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) platform that unifies internal compliance automation and external threat monitoring in a single system of record. Inside the organization, TrustGuard AI continuously collects evidence, maps it to recognized control frameworks — including FedRAMP, SOC 2, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53, NIST CSF, HIPAA, PCI DSS, and CMMC — and uses retrieval-augmented AI to assess controls, surface gaps, draft remediations, and generate audit-ready, machine-readable findings and reports. Looking outward, it delivers continuous third-party and supply-chain risk monitoring, scoring vendors and partners against real-world security signals so teams can quantify exposure, prioritize outreach, and track remediation across their entire ecosystem. By combining automated internal compliance with external security ratings and attack-surface intelligence, TrustGuard AI gives security, risk, and compliance leaders one continuously-updated view of their posture — from their own controls to every vendor they depend on. The platform is offered as SaaS. The provider maintains a SOC 2 Type 2 program and is undergoing a FedRAMP 20x Moderate (Class C) assessment; the FedRAMP-assessed instance operates in production within AWS GovCloud (US).

ConnectSecure LLC's ConnectSecure Vulnerability and Compliance
Manager system. In the service auditor's opinion, in all material respects
and based on the applicable Trust Services Criteria for Security, Availability,

suitably designed to provide reasonable assurance that ConnectSecure's
service commitments and system requirements would be achieved if the
controls operated effectively, and if the subservice organizations and user
entities applied the complementary controls contemplated in the design;
and (3) the controls operated effectively throughout the period. This is an
unqualified opinion with no exceptions noted.

alternativeSecurityFramework.mappingToFedRampRules:
This SOC 2 Type II examination was performed by CertPro CPA LLC under
AICPA attestation standards (AT-C) for the period April 1, 2025 – March 31,
2026, against the 2017 Trust Services Criteria (with 2022 revised points of
focus) for Security, Availability, and Confidentiality. It covered the Common
Criteria (CC1–CC9: control environment, communication and information,
risk assessment, monitoring, control activities, logical and physical access,
system operations, change management, and risk mitigation) plus the
Availability (A1) and Confidentiality (C1) criteria. These map to core
FedRAMP/NIST SP 800-53 control families — Access Control (AC),
Identification & Authentication (IA), Audit & Accountability (AU),
Configuration Management (CM), Contingency Planning (CP), Incident
Response (IR), Risk Assessment (RA), System & Communications
Protection (SC), and System & Information Integrity (SI). The auditor issued
an unqualified opinion: controls were suitably designed and operated
effectively throughout the period with no exceptions noted, and no material
incidents or availability breaches occurred. Independent web-application and
thick-client penetration testing was performed by BDO India LLP
(CREST-accredited) in January 2026, with all findings remediated and
verified closed by February 10, 2026.

trustCenter.accessRequestInstructions:
**Portal access.** Access is granted through a User Access Request (UAR). Your sponsor or point of contact submits the UAR from the Trust Center portal under Request Services; an approver reviews it and the request is tracked as an auditable ticket. Access is removed the same way. You may also self-register from the portal login page (Create New User Account) — a self-registered account is associated with your organization when your email domain matches — but UAR approval is still required before certification data is released. Accounts are role-based and scoped to this system; sensitive fields are excluded from shared reports.

**Programmatic access.** There is no self-service token flow. Submit a service request under Request Services on the same UAR path. Elvo then issues a Client ID and Client Secret scoped to your organization and system, your base URL and tenant identifier, the report ids your organization may pull, and the document retrieval endpoints. Authentication is OAuth2 client_credentials.

**Full instructions:** https://grcitsm.stratuscyber.com/trust-center-access-guide/

The tenant is configured and operated for Elvo by Stratus Cyber LLC. Elvo uses a FedRAMP Certified platform for certification data sharing rather than building and certifying its own. Halo is FedRAMP Certified under package ID FR2621445678 (Type 20x, Path Program, Class C (Moderate), certified 2026-05-06).

Meterbox emphasizes customer data isolation, privacy by default, comprehensive auditability, strong authentication and access controls, flexible deployment for regulated or sovereign environments, and support for privacy and data-rights requirements. The platform is being built toward major enterprise security and compliance standards, while transparently documenting its current certifications, roadmap, security practices, third-party providers, accessibility efforts, and vulnerability-reporting processes.

nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: Transactional delivery is designated for migration to Amazon SES in AWS GovCloud using its FIPS SMTP endpoint.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: Inbound delivery events require signature validation before processing.

nonCertified.potentialImpactToFederalCustomerData: A session could expose purchasing content or supplier credentials if desktop punchout were enabled for a federal organization.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: Kernel-backed desktop punchout is disabled for FedRAMP-enabled organizations.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: The organization-level FedRAMP gate prevents federal sessions from starting in Kernel.

nonCertified.compensatingControls: API and webhook processing enforce the HRIS-only integration boundary.

nonCertified.name: Tailscale

nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: The cryptographic and authorization posture remains subject to a formal FedRAMP suitability decision.
