nonCertified.useCase: Infrastructure state and deployment orchestration.
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration: Pulumi Cloud stores infrastructure state and orchestrates deployments into Silkline environments, including AWS GovCloud.
nonCertified.justification: Silkline uses Pulumi Cloud for reproducible infrastructure management and deployment controls.
nonCertified.potentialImpactToFederalCustomerData: Infrastructure state and deployment authority can affect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of federal workloads.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: The hosting and authorization model remains subject to a formal FedRAMP boundary decision.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: Per-stack identities, encrypted secrets, and short-lived deployment credentials restrict deployment access.

nonCertified.name: GitHub
nonCertified.useCase: Source control, code review, and repository automation.
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration: GitHub hosts source code, pull requests, repository configuration, and automation credentials.
nonCertified.justification: Silkline uses GitHub as the authoritative software-development collaboration platform.
nonCertified.potentialImpactToFederalCustomerData: Repository compromise could introduce code or configuration that affects systems handling federal customer data.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: Repository changes require controlled review and protected-branch workflows.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: Branch protections, CODEOWNERS, access reviews, and required CI checks protect the software supply chain.

nonCertified.name: Depot
nonCertified.useCase: Managed CI runners and container image builds.
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration: Ephemeral Depot runners receive source code and scoped build secrets; selected workflow artifacts are retained for seven days.
nonCertified.justification: Silkline uses Depot to run CI workloads and accelerate container builds.
nonCertified.potentialImpactToFederalCustomerData: Runner compromise could alter build outputs or expose credentials used to deploy systems that handle federal customer data.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: CI workflows use ephemeral runners, short artifact retention, and scoped access to build inputs.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: OIDC supplies short-lived Pulumi access and repository controls require reviewed changes before deployment.

nonCertified.name: Greptile
nonCertified.useCase: Automated code review and repository analysis.
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration: Greptile reads repository source and pull-request context to produce automated review feedback.
nonCertified.justification: Silkline uses Greptile to supplement human code review.
nonCertified.potentialImpactToFederalCustomerData: Repository access could expose source or produce unsafe review advice, but it does not grant deployment authority.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: Greptile output is advisory and changes still pass human review and CI.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: Repository permissions and protected branches prevent the service from directly publishing application changes.

nonCertified.name: Stainless
nonCertified.useCase: Generation of client SDK source code.
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration: Stainless processes API specifications and generates SDK source that is committed to version control.
nonCertified.justification: Silkline uses Stainless to maintain consistent client libraries for its public APIs.
nonCertified.potentialImpactToFederalCustomerData: Generated code could introduce client-side security defects if accepted without review.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: Generated output is reviewed and tested before it is released.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: Committed output passes the same source review and CI controls as maintainer-authored code.

nonCertified.name: Rootly
nonCertified.useCase: Incident workflows, escalation, and response coordination.
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration: Rootly stores incident records, escalation policies, schedules, and response workflow state.
nonCertified.justification: Silkline uses Rootly to coordinate incident response and escalation.
nonCertified.potentialImpactToFederalCustomerData: Incident records can include excerpts or descriptions of affected federal customer content.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: Incident records are limited to the detail required for response and follow-up activities.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: Access is limited to incident responders and workflow notifications use scoped incident context.

nonCertified.name: Slack
nonCertified.useCase: Operational alerting and incident collaboration.
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration: Monitoring and security systems send alert summaries to controlled Slack channels used by responders.
nonCertified.justification: Silkline uses Slack to notify personnel and coordinate operational response.
nonCertified.potentialImpactToFederalCustomerData: Alert payloads or incident discussion can contain limited customer details during diagnosis.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: Alert content is scoped to operational context needed for response.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: Channel membership and workspace access controls limit incident data to authorized personnel.

nonCertified.name: Linear
nonCertified.useCase: Engineering planning and security work tracking.
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration: Linear stores development plans, defect reports, remediation tasks, and security program work items.
nonCertified.justification: Silkline uses Linear to assign and track engineering and compliance work.
nonCertified.potentialImpactToFederalCustomerData: Planning records can reveal architecture or security details that could assist attacks against the service.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: Work items avoid customer content and restrict sensitive details to the minimum needed for remediation.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: Workspace access controls limit records to authorized personnel.

nonCertified.name: Notion
nonCertified.useCase: Internal operational and security documentation.
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration: Notion stores internal documentation, including architecture, boundary, and vendor inventory material.
nonCertified.justification: Silkline uses Notion for collaborative operational documentation.
nonCertified.potentialImpactToFederalCustomerData: Documentation can reveal system design and security decisions relevant to systems that handle federal customer data.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: Documentation excludes federal customer content and separates internal security material from public pages.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: Workspace permissions limit internal documentation to authorized users.

nonCertified.name: Drata
nonCertified.useCase: Compliance evidence and control monitoring.
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration: Drata stores compliance evidence and monitors selected organizational and technical controls.
nonCertified.justification: Silkline uses Drata to support compliance operations and assessments.
nonCertified.potentialImpactToFederalCustomerData: Compliance evidence can reveal control implementation details but does not include federal customer content.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: Evidence collection is scoped to the material required for compliance verification.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: Access controls restrict compliance records to authorized staff and assessors.

nonCertified.name: Paramify
nonCertified.useCase: FedRAMP control implementation and evidence management.
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration: Paramify stores control narratives, component records, mappings, and assessment evidence for the authorization program.
nonCertified.justification: Silkline uses Paramify as the governance workflow for its FedRAMP certification package.
nonCertified.potentialImpactToFederalCustomerData: Authorization records can expose security architecture and affect the accuracy of risk decisions.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: Records are reviewed by assigned control owners and scoped to security and compliance evidence.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: Role-based access and human review govern changes to control evidence.

nonCertified.name: Keeper
nonCertified.useCase: Staff credential and secret management.
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration: Keeper stores staff-managed credentials used to access operational and administrative systems.
nonCertified.justification: Silkline uses Keeper to centralize protected credential storage and sharing.
nonCertified.potentialImpactToFederalCustomerData: Compromised credentials could grant access to systems that handle federal customer data.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: Credential access is limited by workforce role and periodically reviewed.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: SSO, multifactor authentication, and access reviews protect privileged credentials.

nonCertified.name: KnowBe4
nonCertified.useCase: Security awareness training and completion records.
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration: KnowBe4 assigns security training and stores staff training status and completion evidence.
nonCertified.justification: Silkline uses KnowBe4 to operate and evidence its security-awareness program.
nonCertified.potentialImpactToFederalCustomerData: The service handles workforce records but no federal customer content; program failure could weaken personnel security awareness.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: Data is limited to workforce identity and training records.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: Administrative access is restricted and training completion is reviewed.

nonCertified.name: Google Workspace
nonCertified.useCase: Corporate email, identity, documents, and collaboration.
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration: Google Workspace provides staff email, groups, shared documents, and identity services used in company operations.
nonCertified.justification: Silkline uses Google Workspace for workforce communication and collaboration.
nonCertified.potentialImpactToFederalCustomerData: Email or documents can receive federal customer-provided content during support and business communications.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: Staff limit customer content in collaboration tools and use application workflows for operational records.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: Central identity controls, multifactor authentication, and managed groups restrict workforce access.

serviceIdentification.serviceName: Knox Systems FedRAMP High Managed Platform
serviceIdentification.serviceDescription:
Knox Systems provides a multi-tenant cloud platform for delivering commercial software to federal government customers. Customer applications deploy on Knox's managed infrastructure across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud Platform using Kubernetes containers, serverless functions, or virtual machines. Knox provides 24/7 Security Operations Center and Network Operations Center management, continuous security monitoring, vulnerability scanning, patch management, and incident response for all customer workloads. This includes:

Adobe Connect is designed for immersive synchronous online meeting experiences for training, large-scale webinars, and virtual classroom meetings for a distributed workforce.

Backupta is a Resilience Platform for Okta that ensures uninterrupted identity and access management. It delivers secure backup, disaster recovery, and rapid restoration of tenants or objects. Tenant cloning and failover strengthen business continuity, while proactive monitoring and audit logs enhance security.

Peregrine enables public safety and government agencies to integrate, model, and access data from agency and authorized partner systems within a unified platform, allowing information about people, places, and events to be understood in context across systems. Peregrine supports workflows such as search, analysis, reporting, alerting, relationship mapping, and operational monitoring by providing a secure, continuously updated, permission-aware view of agency data for authorized users.

Sift is a SaaS platform for time-series telemetry ingestion, storage, visualization, and rule-based monitoring of mission-critical hardware systems. It serves mission operators, test engineers, and data analysts across federal agencies and their defense and aerospace contractors, providing interactive dashboards and programmatic query access to machine telemetry and associated operational metadata.

Altana Product Network (APN) is a SaaS offering in AWS GovCloud that uses artificial intelligence to create a single source of truth for the global supply chain. It integrates customer and external datasets to map suppliers, shipments, compliance, and risk, and is used by customer administrators and end users through a web portal with SAML 2.0 federation. The boundary is supported by EKS-based microservices, Databricks data pipelines, and core AWS services such as RDS, S3, OpenSearch, and ElastiCache.

Sierra is a multi-tenant SaaS Cloud Service Offering (CSO) that enables Federal agencies to build, deploy, and operate conversational AI agents that interact with the agency's constituents and employees across chat, voice, email, and other channels primarily to handle customer support, case intake, benefits inquiries, and similar service workflows autonomously so agencies can resolve high-volume citizen interactions at scale economically.

The Acsense IAM Resilience Platform is a cloud-based SaaS solution that serves as an Identity Control Plane, providing unified backup & recovery, disaster recovery on a separate remote tenant, configuration management, and compliance assurance capabilities for enterprise identity and access management (IAM) environments. The platform is IDP-agnostic by design, primarily supporting both Okta (Workforce and CIAM) and Microsoft Entra ID deployments.The system enables authorized administrators to back up enterprise identity infrastructure (including human and non-human identities/machine identities), track and compare configuration changes with full role attribution, map dependencies, detect configuration drift in approximately 10 minutes, and leverage Continuous Resilience Validation to ensure a tested ~10-minute Recovery Time Objective (RTO) during operational incidents, ransomware attacks, or outages. The authorization boundary includes the Acsense SaaS application, supporting management services, application APIs, data processing services, and storage components operated in cloud infrastructure environments. The platform is used by enterprise and government administrators, security teams, and IT operations personnel to process identity-related business data and limited personally identifiable information (PII) associated with IAM objects and user accounts. The service is delivered as a multi-tenant SaaS platform with customer-isolated data storage (or as a single, separated tenant) and relies on external identity provider APIs and cloud infrastructure services to perform authorized backup, synchronization, monitoring, and recovery operations.

Swimlane's Turbine is a multi-tenant SaaS agentic AI security automation platform which uses low-code technology to unify disparate cybersecurity tools into a centralized system of action. By utilizing agentic AI (Hero AI) alongside a visual, drag-and-drop playbook builder, the platform automates complex Security Operations Center (SOC) workflows, vulnerability management, and incident triage without requiring extensive custom coding. This comprehensive AI SOC orchestration eliminates alert fatigue for security teams, tracks compliance, and provides real-time ROI reporting to accelerate threat responses and protect large organizations globally.

Determinate is an SDLC collaboration and deployment automation platform. It specifically caters to the Nix ecosystem for reproducible and declarative software projects. Determinate processes and delivers software source code (FlakeHub, a source artifact repository) and compiled artifacts (FlakeHub Cache, a binary artifact repository) to end users as multi-tenant SaaS. Users publish their software via the customer's coding forge, like GitHub or GitLab.

The Vannevar platform supports government agencies and other authorized government users by running guided, agent-assisted workflows across disparate datasets and proprietary data to reduce the time required to turn raw information into investigative outputs. Within the platform, users can ingest and analyze digital artifacts and other government-provided data, correlate and search across those sources, and leverage agents to generate consistent work products. These workflows enable digital forensic sensemaking, investigative development and enrichment, and the production of shareable products for downstream action.

Tractian is an asset health monitoring platform that gives government agencies the intelligence to keep critical physical assets running in support of mission readiness, with security and compliance built for U.S. federal requirements. Wireless sensors and AI analytics support the whole asset health lifecycle, detecting developing failures, tracking how they progress, and guiding teams through to resolution before an issue becomes downtime or a safety event. The platform is deployed within Knox's FedRAMP High Authorized environment on AWS GovCloud, and it helps agencies and contractors get more output and reliability from the equipment they already have, without adding headcount, capital expense, or new risk.

MissionML Studio is a platform used to build, prototype, and productionize AI-enabled government workflow applications and securely host and monitor them. It is deployed as a secure, fully managed, single-tenant cloud platform where government program managers build and prototype custom AI workflow applications tailored to their mission needs and process operational, analytical, and mission data, while ensuring isolation for each customer environment.

Vectra AI delivers AI-native security and observability that helps federal security teams build and demonstrate resilience against modern cyber threats. The platform provides unified observability across on-premises networks, identity, cloud, SaaS, IoT/OT, edge, and AI infrastructure to identify active threats, prioritize investigation and response, and help agencies proactively reduce cyber risk and strengthen security posture. Federal security analysts, incident responders, administrators, and security leaders use the platform to monitor activity, investigate suspicious behavior, hunt for threats, contain compromised identities or devices, and assess gaps in security coverage. The platform provides contextual investigation, natural-language assistance, attack-path visualization, operational reporting, and evidence that supports continuous monitoring, compliance, and SOC optimization. More than 2,000 organizations use Vectra AI, which was named a Leader in the 2025 and 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Network Detection and Response.

Upwind Security is a SaaS cloud security platform that enables authorized users to identify and manage cloud vulnerabilities, security misconfigurations, runtime threats, and cloud asset inventory within cloud environments. The authorization boundary includes the Upwind application and supporting services necessary to provide these capabilities, processes cloud infrastructure metadata and security telemetry, and relies on AWS GovCloud (US) infrastructure and authorized external service dependencies to deliver the service.

SimpliGov is a cloud-based, multi-tenant Software-as-a-Service application that provides a government operations platform used by state and local agencies to design, run, and improve how their programs operate: digital forms that capture program data, and automation that moves applications, approvals, documents, signatures, and payments across teams and systems. The platform is used by more than 100 agencies and is sold only to U.S. public-sector customers.

serviceIdentification.serviceDescription: 2F Game Warden is a fully managed and compliant multi-tenant DevSecOps platform that accelerates the delivery of commercial cloud software to federal government customers, State, Local, and Education (SLED) agencies, and highly regulated industries. Engineered to support dual compliance pathways, Game Warden can be leveraged as a pre-authorized FedRAMP PaaS for external systems or utilized for fully in-boundary application hosting, granting customers an inherited FedRAMP certification. Built to provide Fort Knox level infrastructure security, customer workloads deploy natively on our managed infrastructure across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud Platform (GCP) utilizing Kubernetes containers, serverless functions, or virtual machines. The platform fully automates continuous monitoring, threat mitigation, vulnerability scanning, patch management, and control inheritance required to conform to strict FedRAMP High, DoD IL5, and GovRAMP standards. Second Front Systems handles 100% of the underlying infrastructure maintenance, enabling commercial SaaS technology to rapidly scale across public sector and regulated missions without the overhead of building traditional compliance frameworks from scratch.

serviceIdentification.serviceDescription:
Dayforce HCM, Public Sector (Dayforce Pub Sec) is a Software as a Service (SaaS) Human Capital Management (HCM) cloud service offering deployed in a public cloud environment for use by U.S. Federal Government agencies. The service provides integrated capabilities for human resources, payroll, workforce management, benefits administration, document management, employee communications, analytics, reporting, and secure application integration through a single logical application platform.

The FedRAMP authorization boundary includes the Dayforce Pub Sec application services, management services, identity and access management services, document management services, integration services, messaging services, analytics services, and supporting cloud platform components required to deliver the service. Only those services, features, and components included within the authorization boundary have been independently assessed as part of the FedRAMP Moderate authorization.

The service supports federated identity using customer-managed identity providers and implements Digital Identity Level 2 (IAL2/AAL2) requirements, including multifactor authentication and identity federation, as applicable. The service employs role-based access control, privileged access management, centralized audit logging, continuous monitoring, vulnerability management, incident response, and FIPS 140-3 validated cryptographic modules to protect federal information in transit and at rest.

Dayforce Pub Sec is designed to process, store, and transmit Federal Moderate impact information, including Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), in accordance with FIPS PUB 199 Moderate security requirements. Security responsibilities are shared between Dayforce and customer agencies as defined in the Customer Responsibility Matrix, with customer organizations responsible for agency-managed identity governance, endpoint security, and organization-specific security controls.

certified.useCase:
Resource Name: Amazon Web Services (AWS Commercial)
General Usage & Configuration: Cloud Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) and Platform as a Service (PaaS) configured using AWS Organizations, IAM Identity Center, isolated VPCs, and centralized encryption.
Justification for Use: Delivers scalable, highly available compute, storage, networking, and managed database services to host critical workloads.
Mitigation Measures: Implement AWS KMS encryption at rest and in transit, GuardDuty threat monitoring, CloudTrail audit logging, AWS WAF, and multi-factor authentication for all IAM identities.
Compensating Controls: AWS Control Tower posture guardrails, automated compliance drift evaluation via AWS Config, and mandatory egress filtering through centralized firewalls.

Resource Name: Paramify Cloud
General Usage & Configuration: Automated cybersecurity documentation and GRC platform configured to auto-generate and maintain OSCAL-based System Security Plans (SSPs) and compliance artifacts.
Justification for Use: Automates compliance documentation drafting for NIST SP 800-53 and FedRAMP baselines, reducing manual oversight and documentation drift.
Mitigation Measures: Enforce RBAC for platform access, mandate SSO/MFA for all users, enforce AES-256 encryption at rest for generated compliance files, and sanitize operational details.
Compensating Controls: Internal technical lead and CISO manual sign-off on all system boundaries, control implementations, and generated SSP artifacts before submission.

nonCertified.name: 1Password
nonCertified.useCase:
General Usage & Configuration: Enterprise credential vault and secret management configured with zero-knowledge encryption, enforced Master Password + Secret Key policies, mandatory MFA, and role-based vault segregation.
Justification for Use: Centralizes credential management, prevents plain-text secret storage, and eliminates risky password-reuse practices across administrative and operational teams.
Mitigation Measures: Enforce zero-knowledge architecture, continuous device trust validation, admin IP allowlisting, and automated secret rotation schedules.
Compensating Controls: Mandatory integration with primary Identity Provider (SSO) for automated user provisioning/deprovisioning; secret access auditing via SIEM ingestion.

nonCertified.name: 3rd Degree
nonCertified.useCase:
General Usage & Configuration: Pre-employment background verification and identity screening platform configured with encrypted candidate invite links and policy-driven adjudication workflows.
Justification for Use: Verifies candidate background, credentials, and legal eligibility to mitigate insider threat risks before granting access to corporate infrastructure.
Mitigation Measures: Limit PII exposure via strict Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), enforce TLS 1.3 in transit and AES-256 at rest, enforce strict data retention schedules, and execute DPAs/BAAs.
Compensating Controls: HR and Legal double-check and sign off on screening results before access is granted; zero system access or account creation prior to background clearance.

nonCertified.name: A-LIGN
nonCertified.useCase:
General Usage & Configuration: Automated compliance management and audit portal (A-SCEND) configured for automated evidence collection, continuous control monitoring, and audit submission.
Justification for Use: Streamlines SOC 2, ISO 27001, and FedRAMP assessment workflows, centralizing audit artifacts and continuous posture evaluation.
Mitigation Measures: Restrict portal access to compliance staff via SSO/MFA, apply least-privilege read-only permissions to audit integrations, and scrub sensitive PII/PHI from uploaded artifacts.
Compensating Controls: Continuous manual review of all compliance evidence prior to auditor release; annual review of A-LIGN’s SOC 2 Type II assessment reports.

nonCertified.name: Atlassian (Confluence & Jira)
nonCertified.useCase:
General Usage & Configuration: Enterprise cloud documentation knowledge base and issue tracking configured with SAML 2.0 SSO, strict space/project permissions, and encrypted storage.
Justification for Use: Centralizes compliance policy management, technical documentation, and security ticket tracking across operational teams.
Mitigation Measures: Enforce OneLogin SSO with hardware-token MFA, restrict public space/project sharing, enforce IP allowlisting, and sanitize sensitive PII/PHI from wiki pages.
Compensating Controls: Mandatory SIEM log ingestion for admin activity; annual SOC 2 Type II review of Atlassian Cloud controls.

nonCertified.name: Google Workspace
nonCertified.useCase:
General Usage & Configuration: Cloud productivity, corporate email (Gmail), and document collaboration (Drive) configured with Client-Side Encryption (CSE), context-aware access controls, and strict DLP rules.
Justification for Use: Provides enterprise email, communication, and document sharing required for business operations.
Mitigation Measures: Enforce SSO with hardware-token MFA, implement strict Data Loss Prevention (DLP) rules blocking external sharing of sensitive data, and restrict OAuth app authorizations.
Compensating Controls: Endpoint detection and response (EDR) software on all enterprise devices; continuous automated email security gateway scanning to filter phishing attempts.

nonCertified.name: Ninjio
nonCertified.useCase:
General Usage & Configuration: Security awareness micro-learning and phishing simulation platform configured with automated monthly training modules and simulated phishing campaigns.
Justification for Use: Strengthens staff defense mechanisms against social engineering, phishing, and malware threats, ensuring compliance with federal awareness standards.
Mitigation Measures: Anonymize user profiles using minimal PII (email/pseudonym only) during account provisioning; enforce strict administrative SSO access.
Compensating Controls: Automated email security gateways (e.g., Defender for Office 365 / Proofpoint) that analyze, neutralize, and quarantine real-world threats independently of user action.

nonCertified.name: OneLogin
nonCertified.useCase:
General Usage & Configuration: Enterprise Identity and Access Management (IAM) and Single Sign-On (SSO) solution configured with Adaptive MFA, SAML 2.0/OIDC integrations, and automated SCIM provisioning.
Justification for Use: Centralizes user identity authentication, access enforcement, and automated user lifecycle management across all corporate SaaS and cloud systems.
Mitigation Measures: Require step-up Adaptive MFA based on risk scoring, enforce robust password complexity guidelines, limit session durations, and forward auth logs to a SIEM.
Compensating Controls: Secured break-glass administrative credentials maintained in offline physical vaults; baseline access policies for critical infrastructure when SSO is unreachable.

nonCertified.name: OpenVPN Server
nonCertified.useCase:
General Usage & Configuration: Centralized Virtual Private Network host application managing encrypted tunnel connections configured with TLS 1.3, AES-256-GCM, and client certificate authentication.
Justification for Use: Grants encrypted, authenticated remote access to private corporate networks and non-public cloud infrastructure for remote staff.
Mitigation Measures: Enforce multi-factor authentication alongside key-based client certificates, restrict split tunneling, enforce tight firewall rules on VPN gateways, and log session data.
Compensating Controls: Network-level micro-segmentation limiting VPN client routing exclusively to authorized IP ranges and application ports based on user role.

nonCertified.name: Terraform
nonCertified.useCase:
General Usage & Configuration: Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) tool (CLI/Cloud) configured to manage cloud resource provisioning, utilizing remote state locking and encrypted backend storage.
Justification for Use: Enables repeatable, version-controlled, and audited infrastructure deployments, reducing human configuration error.
Mitigation Measures: Encrypt state files at rest using KMS AES-256, restrict state file access strictly to CI/CD service accounts, scan code for secrets/misconfigurations prior to commit, and require peer code reviews.
Compensating Controls: Separation of duties preventing developers from directly applying infrastructure changes; all executions must run through isolated, audited CI/CD pipelines.

nonCertified.name: Twilio
nonCertified.useCase:
General Usage & Configuration: Cloud communications platform configured for programmatic SMS messaging, system status alerts, and multi-factor authentication token delivery via REST APIs.
Justification for Use: Enables automated application-to-person notifications, out-of-band verification codes, and real-time operational status alerts.
Mitigation Measures: Enforce strict TLS API communication, scope API tokens to minimum required capabilities, implement strict rate-limiting, and validate incoming webhooks via digital signatures.
Compensating Controls: Offer secondary/fallback out-of-band authentication methods (e.g., TOTP authenticator apps, WebAuthn push notifications) to mitigate SIM-swapping risks inherent to SMS.

nonCertified.name: Udemy Business
nonCertified.useCase:

Justification for Use: Provides ongoing technical skill development, cybersecurity training courses, and professional development for staff.
Mitigation Measures: Enforce SSO/MFA authentication, restrict public course publishing from enterprise accounts, and minimize shared account details to essential attributes (Name/Work Email).
Compensating Controls: Corporate endpoint isolation and web filtering policies preventing personal web activity or file downloads from impacting enterprise networks.

serviceIdentification.serviceDescription:
The Anomali Cloud Service Offering consists of two integrated components: Security Analytics and ThreatStream, delivered as a unified cloud-native security platform. Security Analytics provides AI and cloud-native security information and event management (SIEM) capabilities including data collection and normalization from network devices, endpoints, applications, and cloud services; real-time event correlation and threat detection using machine learning algorithms; behavioral analytics and anomaly detection; incident response workflows; and query capabilities across petabytes of historical data stored in an integrated security data lake with configurable retention periods up to 7+ years. The platform supports ingestion of 30TB+ of data within hours and enables sub-second query response times across petabyte-scale datasets using natural language processing and AI-supported interfaces.

ThreatStream provides threat intelligence management capabilities including automated collection, normalization, and curation of threat intelligence from commercial feeds, open source intelligence, and information sharing centers; management of indicators of compromise (IOCs) and indicators of attack (IOAs) with automated deduplication and confidence scoring; correlation of external threat intelligence with internal security telemetry; distribution of actionable intelligence to integrated security tools via APIs and standard protocols; threat analysis and enrichment with MITRE ATT&CK framework mapping; and secure community-based threat sharing. The service operates as a multi-tenant Software-as-a-Service solution with role-based access controls, data encryption in transit and at rest, comprehensive audit logging, and RESTful APIs for integration with existing security infrastructure. Service boundaries include all data ingestion interfaces, processing engines, storage systems, user interfaces, APIs, and integration points necessary to deliver security analytics and threat intelligence management capabilities.

The Collaborative Learning Environment (CLE) is a full-featured, end-to-end virtual school platform for managing learning, providing brick-and-mortar-like classroom experiences using audio, video, live collaboration tools and asynchronous tools and LMS capabilities.
System capabilities include:
- Real-time collaboration with audio, video, shared content, and recording capabilities
- User management
- Reporting and data analysis
- Classroom management including assignments, evaluations, and grading
- Central repository for media and other shared materials with the ability to build and edit course materials from a single workspace

serviceIdentification.serviceDescription: VulcanGov (Justinian for Government) is a SaaS AI platform for government: an AI agent workspace grounded in a curated, continuously updated library of federal and state statutes, regulations, guidance and housing datasets, with full-text and semantic search, secure single-use agent sandboxes for code execution and document generation, and an administration console for agency user management, session audit visibility and usage export. It is delivered from a government-only environment in AWS GovCloud (US) (us-gov-east-1) on a containerized microservices architecture: AWS ECS Fargate, Aurora PostgreSQL, S3 object storage, OpenSearch and ElastiCache. Federal customer data is stored and processed in AWS GovCloud (US); large language model inference is provided by Amazon Bedrock through a documented transport bridge, and every cross-boundary resource, including any temporary deviation, is disclosed in the published third-party information resources and service-scope lists rather than omitted. Data is encrypted at rest (AWS KMS, AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2/1.3) with FIPS 140-validated cryptographic modules; identity and access are federated through Okta for Government with enforced multi-factor authentication; security monitoring uses Datadog for Government, Wiz for Government and native AWS security services. Available to federal, state and local governments and to organizations working on their behalf. Public offering information, the secure configuration guide and live availability status are published on the Trust Center at https://trust.vulcangov.app; FedRAMP Certification Data is available to federal reviewers through its gated portal.

TrackVia is an AI ready Operational Intelligence Platform that helps government agencies and organizations turn complex, mission critical operations into structured data, automated workflows, real time intelligence, and measurable outcomes.

Rather than relying on spreadsheets, disconnected point solutions, or lengthy custom software development, organizations use TrackVia to rapidly configure and deploy operational applications around their unique mission and business requirements. TrackVia brings workflows, data, automation, mobile capabilities, integrations, and AI together in a secure, governed platform.

TrackVia supports use cases including field operations, inspections, workforce and mission readiness, asset and equipment management, safety and compliance, program operations, contractor and vendor management, and other mission critical workflows.

TrackVia Government provides federal agencies and government contractors a secure path to modernize operational processes while meeting stringent federal security and compliance requirements.

**Remedio: correction beats visibility. Find it, fix it, prove it — at machine speed.**

Remedio is a configuration-focused device hardening and autonomous remediation offering that finds, fixes, and verifies security misconfigurations, unpatched vulnerabilities, unauthorized applications, and unmanaged AI tools across agency endpoints and servers, wherever they run — on premises, remote, or in the cloud. Hardening continues off-network, indefinitely.

Remedio closes the loop between detection and correction by applying policy-controlled, automated fixes and giving administrators an instant, auditable rollback path for every change. This lets government security teams enforce baselines like DISA STIG, NIST 800-53, and CIS Benchmarks continuously — not just at audit time — while reducing the manual workload historically required to close configuration and compliance gaps at scale.

**Core capabilities**

1. **Remedio Baseline — configuration hardening.** Establishes and continuously enforces secure configuration baselines (Golden Images) across Windows, Linux, and macOS endpoints and servers, automatically correcting drift as it occurs.
2. **Remedio Fortify — vulnerability and misconfiguration remediation.** Identifies and prioritizes vulnerabilities and misconfigurations, then applies safe, automated remediation at scale to reduce patch and hardening backlogs.
3. **Remedio Assure — continuous compliance.** Continuously validates configuration and remediation state against required control frameworks and agency-specific policy, maintaining audit-ready evidence and full traceability for oversight and reporting.
4. **Remedio Gate — application control.** Discovers and controls installed software, scripts, and services, blocking unauthorized or risky applications, browser plugins, and dev-tool extensions before they create exposure.
5. **Remedio AI Govern — shadow AI governance.** Discovers and governs AI tools, models, agents, and connected integrations in use across the environment, bringing shadow AI into visibility and enforcing approved-use policy and access controls.

**How it works**

Each Remedio capability operates on a continuous cycle: **Review** (aggregate device state against secure baselines), **Reveal** (surface misconfigurations, identity gaps, and shadow AI usage), **Reassess** (ongoing validation against baselines and compliance mandates), **Remediate** (apply policy-controlled fixes, closing findings as they are detected rather than waiting on manual ticket cycles), and **Revert** (instant rollback of any change if conditions require). The cycle runs on the device itself, so scanning and remediation continue while a device is off the network, and findings upload when it reconnects. Every remediation action is logged for audit and reporting purposes, and the platform includes built-in ROI reporting to quantify time saved, risk reduced, and compliance gains.

Live evidence: [Trust Center](https://trust.remedio.io) · [Secure Configuration Guide](https://trust.remedio.io/scg) · [Certification progress](https://trust.remedio.io/progress) · [remedio.io](https://remedio.io)

serviceIdentification.serviceDescription:
Cloudflare operates a global network that delivers security, performance, and reliability from a single platform. Cloudflare for Government provides this same platform to U.S. Government agencies as one homogeneous stack. This Marketplace listing consolidates both of Cloudflare for Government's FedRAMP Certifications — Class C (previously FedRAMP Moderate) and Class D (previously FedRAMP High) — into a single product entry. The certified services span:

- **SASE / Zero Trust** — Zero Trust network access, secure web gateway, CASB, browser isolation, data loss prevention, email security, and cloud-delivered WAN.
- **Security** — web application firewall (WAF), DDoS protection, API security, bot management, rate limiting, and client-side security.
- **Network & Content Delivery** — CDN, authoritative DNS, load balancing, smart routing, and network interconnect.
- **Compute** — serverless functions, containers, durable objects, and workflow orchestration.
- **Storage** — object storage, SQL and key-value databases, and queues.

Federal agencies use Cloudflare to protect public-facing websites and APIs, secure workforce access to internal applications, replace legacy remote-access VPN and MPLS connectivity, and build cloud-native applications entirely within the FedRAMP-certified boundary.

The two Certifications are delivered from separate environments with separate control planes. Class C is accessed at dash.cloudflare.com and api.cloudflare.com; Class D is accessed at dash.fed.cloudflare.com and api.fed.cloudflare.com. Federal customers select the environment that matches the FedRAMP Certification required for their workload.

This offering is FedRAMP Class C and Class D Certified. The scope of the two Certifications differs by a small number of services; per-service class is denoted in the Certified Services list as follows: services with no notation are Certified at both Class C and Class D, services marked with an asterisk (*) are Certified at Class C only (not within the Class D boundary), and services marked with a dagger (†) are Certified at Class D only (not within the Class C boundary). Learn more at https://www.cloudflare.com/public-sector/

serviceIdentification.serviceDescription:
Constellation GovCloud (CGC) is an information system that provides the necessary Platform as a Service (PaaS) architecture layers to support Merlin-operated Software as a Service (SaaS) applications. These Merlin SaaS applications will be hosted and provided to U.S. federal agencies, including local and state governments and tribal organizations. The CGC is part of a managed service that is designed to accelerate FedRAMP authorizations allowing Merlin SaaS companies to achieve a FedRAMP Authority to Operate (ATO) more quickly and cost-effectively.

**Services undergoing approval for use — not authorized.** The following services are hosted on CGC but are **not** authorized services and are **not** included in this certification. They are undergoing approval for use and are recorded here for transparency only; neither is covered by this package, and each moves into the certified service list only on completion of that approval.

- **Torq AI SOC Platform** — Torq combines agentic insights and automation so that federal agencies and public sector organizations can triage, investigate, and respond to actual risks, faster. Torq streamlines every step from alert through resolution, expanding capacity and throughput. First, Torq ingests and normalizes telemetry from across your security stack, preparing the data for agentic reasoning at scale. Auto Triage filters out noise and prioritizes actual threats. Next, cases are automatically opened and assigned to highly specialized AI agents designed for investigation and response. Using tools and actions you specify, they gather evidence, assemble timelines, and transparently record decisions and authorized actions. Your team is in complete control. With Torq, your SOC delivers more results, more efficiently, from triage through remediation.

- **QIZ** — QIZ delivers a cloud-based cryptography posture management platform for government agencies and regulated organizations to manage cryptographic risk. The system provides centralized capabilities for cryptographic discovery and inventory, correlation of findings to affected systems and owners, policy definition, risk-based triage, root cause analysis, and remediation planning. QIZ collects cryptographic data from network traffic, system and application configurations, source code, binaries, and cloud infrastructure. Cryptographic standards are defined within the platform, and the system evaluates the environment against those standards to report current posture and identify policy violations. QIZ produces a contextualized cryptographic bill of materials (CBOM), exportable in standard formats, and a policy driven transition plan prioritized by risk and business context, giving agencies a sequenced and repeatable path toward post-quantum readiness.

certifiedServices.serviceDescription: Cynamics, a leading innovator in network cybersecurity, presents a next-generation SOC AI platform powered by its proprietary sample-based NDR and cybersecurity large language model, CynLLM. By integrating intelligent sampling with cutting-edge AI, Cynamics facilitates real-time and scalable threat detection without the heavy infrastructure requirements of traditional solutions. Already endorsed by Tier-1 municipalities, enterprises, and critical infrastructure providers globally, Cynamics offers unparalleled visibility, automation, and operational efficiency for today's security teams.

Hyperproof delivers a modern, cloud-based compliance operations platform designed to help government agencies and regulated organizations manage risk and compliance with confidence. Hyperproof Gov is a cloud-based governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) platform designed to support regulated organizations in managing security and compliance programs. The system provides centralized capabilities for control management, evidence collection, risk tracking, audit support, and continuous monitoring. Hyperproof Gov enables structured workflows and real-time compliance status reporting to support authorization, assessment, and ongoing monitoring activities. The platform is designed to integrate with external systems for automated evidence collection and to maintain traceability between controls, requirements, and supporting artifacts, supporting consistent and repeatable compliance operations.

InfoSec Global Federal's AgileSec Analytics provides automated discovery, monitoring, and policy-driven control of cryptographic assets, including keys, certificates, algorithms, libraries, devices, applications, firmware, and protocols, across cloud and on-premise environments. The AgileSec Analytics platform ensures agencies are prepared for emerging cryptographic threats, including quantum attacks, by monitoring usage of cryptography and preparing migration to post-quantum cryptography. Key capabilities include Automated Cryptographic Discovery & Inventory, Vulnerability Identification and Compliance Reporting, Post-Quantum Readiness, and Continuous Monitoring and Remediation Workflows. The AgileSec Analytics solution supports regulatory requirements including OMB 23-02 mandates and continuous diagnostics, with built-in reporting features evaluated and recognized by federal standards organizations. It also integrates with numerous ecosystem technologies including EDR, CLM, PKI, HSM, CDM dashboards, ITSM, GRC tools and more.

serviceIdentification.serviceDescription: Cohesity helps public sector agencies strengthen cyber resilience through a compliance-focused portfolio of cloud data protection and recovery services. Cohesity Cloud Services for Government brings together secure backup, rapid recovery, centralized management, and cyber vaulting in a streamlined service experience, helping agencies reduce operational complexity, protect mission-critical data, and recover with confidence from ransomware and other disruptive events. The portfolio includes Cohesity DataProtect and Helios for Government capabilities, as well as FortKnox SaaS vaults for DataProtect. FortKnox provides Cohesity-managed cyber vaulting that helps isolate backup data from production environments, with cold- and warm-tier vaulting options, anomaly-detection reporting, and flexible recovery capabilities. Together, these offerings give public sector agencies a scalable way to modernize data protection, improve resilience, and support mission continuity.

recommendation, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) workloads. Customers create
indexes in a cloud region of their choosing and interact with the service through
documented APIs and client SDKs. The service is operated by Pinecone on public cloud
infrastructure, with customer data encrypted at rest (AES-256, unique per-customer keys)
and in transit (TLS 1.2 minimum).

Agentic AI platform developed by ThinkTrends LLC. It
provides federal agencies and commercial organizations with

intelligent workflows. Key capabilities include:
- **AI Agent Studio**: Build and deploy conversational AI
agents with RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation), memory,
and tool integrations backed by Amazon foundation models.
- **Knowledge Base Management**: Ingest, index, and query
structured and unstructured documents using vector
embeddings for grounded, citation-based AI responses.
- **Agent Flow Orchestration**: Design and execute visual
node-based AI workflows for automated, multi-step tasks.
- **Data Pipelines**: Managed Agentic ETL-based pipelines
for data ingestion, transformation, and delivery.
- **Guardrails & Safety**: Configurable content safety
guardrails (HIPAA, PII, tone, compliance policies) applied at
the agent and platform level.
- **File & Drive Integration**: Secure file management
integrated with Google Drive and native cloud storage.
- **Enterprise Connectors**: Native integrations with Slack,
Jira, Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, and agency
enterprise systems.
- **Agentic Governance**: Ability to run automated evaluation
jobs, analyse agent responses against accuracy, relevance,
and safety benchmarks, and iteratively improve prompts
based on those scores

serviceIdentification.serviceDescription: TNT is a multi-tenant, cloud-hosted (SaaS) platform for continuous security testing and compliance management. Core capabilities: (1) automated, authorized penetration testing and adversary emulation against customer-designated in-scope targets; (2) asset discovery and inventory with vulnerability aggregation and risk scoring; (3) governance, risk, and compliance monitoring that maps findings and evidence to frameworks such as NIST SP 800-53, PCI DSS, HIPAA, CIS Controls, and SOC 2 and reports control gaps with remediation guidance; and (4) security reporting and dashboards. An optional lightweight TNT endpoint sensor forwards host security telemetry to the platform's cloud analysis services for continuous analysis and threat hunting. The TNT Business Resilience Platform also integrates Agger ransomware protection capabilities, including endpoint-based behavioral detection, prevention, and response. Applicable cloud services supporting these capabilities are incorporated into the TNT service architecture and FedRAMP assessment scope. Automated assessment and analysis are performed by AI agents operating under human supervision.

Cisco Cloud Control with AgenticOps
Cisco Cloud Control with AgenticOps serves as the autonomous control
plane for hybrid cloud environments. By integrating "AgenticOps"—a
framework of specialized, task-oriented AI agents—the system moves
beyond traditional automation into autonomous remediation and lifecycle
management. It is designed to handle complex compliance requirements by
enabling agents to autonomously detect drift, perform vulnerability
remediation, and ensure that infrastructure state remains continuously
aligned with defined security policies.
Cisco Cloud Control is the unified management and orchestration platform
for hybrid and multi-cloud environments. It acts as the central plane for
governing, securing, and operating distributed infrastructure, providing
consistent policy enforcement and lifecycle automation across disparate
cloud services and data centers. By centralizing management, it eliminates
operational silos, streamlines compliance, and ensures that infrastructure
remains performant and secure at scale.
The Rich Suite of Offers
To support the autonomous capabilities of Cloud Control, the following
products integrate into a cohesive operational ecosystem:
1. AI Canvas
● Description: The design and orchestration workbench for the
AgenticOps ecosystem. AI Canvas provides a visual interface for
engineering teams to design, model, and deploy autonomous agents.
It allows for the mapping of complex operational workflows into
executable logic, ensuring that agents are constrained by well-defined
operational boundaries before they are deployed to manage
production environments.
2. AI Assistant
● Description: The natural language operational interface for the suite.
AI Assistant bridges the gap between human intent and machine
execution. It enables engineers to query system status, request
complex remediation tasks, or gain insights into compliance posture
through conversational interactions. It serves as the primary gateway
for users to interface with the autonomous agents created in AI
Canvas.
3. Cisco IQ
● Description: The centralized intelligence and observability engine.
Cisco IQ processes massive streams of telemetry data from across
the cloud infrastructure to provide actionable insights. It serves as the
"brain" for the agents, providing the contextual data required for
informed decision-making, trend analysis, and predictive modeling,
ensuring that operational actions are grounded in current, real-time
data.
4. AI Defense
● Description: The dedicated security layer for the AI model pipeline
and agentic infrastructure. AI Defense provides the necessary
guardrails to protect AI models from adversarial manipulation, data
leakage, and unauthorized access. In high-compliance environments,
it ensures that the models driving the agents are hardened, verifiable,
and protected against vulnerabilities that could compromise the
integrity of the automated security remediation processes.

Details Analysis/ Evidence of Automation (KSI Focus)
The FedRAMP 20x rules heavily emphasize Persistent and Automated activities.
● Strengths: AI Defense SOC 2 report confirms the use of Datadog for
availability monitoring (CCF-STA-03.02) and Jenkins/ArgoCD for automated
CI/CD pipeline validation (CCF-CCC-04.02).
● FedRAMP 20x Class A requires the JSON schema output for these
activities. AI Defense SOC 2 proves the existence of the control; AI Defense
will ensure these tools output to the specific FedRAMP JSON schema
.
required by FRC-CSO-JSN
Penetration Testing Requirements
● Rule: FRC-CLA-MFR mandates annual penetration testing
(CCF-TVM-02.02 in your SOC 2).
● AI Defense SOC 2 report confirms annual pen testing was performed.
Data Flow and Scope
● Rule: MAS-CSO-IIR requires a machine-readable inventory of all information
resources.
● AI Defense have CCF-DSP-01.02 (Inventory maintenance)
and CCF-DSP-02.02 (Data flow documentation). Since these already exist in
Defense SOC 2 description, the LOE for this requirement is
primarily formatting (mapping current inventory artifacts into the FedRAMP
JSON/OSCAL structure) which is done at time of submission to FedRAMP.
Additional Notes on Implementations
● JSON Schema Mapping (FRC-CSO-JSN & CDS-CSO-PUB): Defense SOC 2
report contains rich control evidence. The biggest lift for Class A is moving
from documentary evidence (PDFs) to structured data (JSON/OSCAL). Defense
Compliance team will export existing audit logs from Splunk and AWS CloudTrail
directly into the FedRAMP JSON schema format defined in the ruleset.
● Addressing "New" Requirements: Rules like AFC-CSO-INB (Security Inbox)
and CDS-CSO-UTC (Trust Center) are not typically found in SOC 2 reports.
These are operational requirements. Since Cisco AI Defense already has an
established Incident Response and Communication procedure (CCF-SEF-01.01),
AI Defense leverages existing communication protocols and use
the fedramp_security@cisco.com alias to satisfy this rule.
● Refining "Persistent" Indicators: Several rules require "persistent" verification
(e.g., KSI-CNA-MAT, KSI-CNA-RNT). AI Defense’s SOC 2 audit tested these on
an annual or quarterly basis. To satisfy 20x, cadence is persistently (e.g.,
automated weekly check) and ensure Datadog or AWS Security Hub configuration
snapshots document this frequency.
Agency Use Case: MKT-IIP-AGU. SOC 2 confirms the AI Defense System is
designed to identify and manage AI model risks across distributed environments. This
is AI Defense’s "Direct Use" case justification for the FedRAMP marketplace listing.

certifiedServices.serviceDescription:
Security Cloud Control is Cisco’s unified, cloud-native security management
interface for the Cisco Security Cloud. It simplifies and strengthens
defenses by centralizing security solutions into a single, cohesive interface.
This approach eliminates silos, reduces complexity, and provides
end-to-end visibility, empowering organizations to proactively address
security

Cisco AI Defense is a comprehensive AI security solution designed to
secure AI models, applications, and agents throughout their lifecycle. It
provides continuous discovery of AI assets such as models, agents, and
datasets across cloud environments including AWS. The service detects
vulnerabilities through automated model validation, supply chain scanning,
and algorithmic red teaming. It protects AI workloads at runtime with
guardrails that block harmful inputs and outputs, preventing threats like
prompt injection, data leakage, and unsafe agent behavior.

AI Canvas is a shared operational workspace where people and AI agents
work together to investigate and resolve IT issues.
An investigation in AI Canvas can bring together information from Cisco
products and integrated third-party systems—such as monitoring,
incident-management, security, automation, and knowledge-management
tools—along with uploaded files, organizational knowledge, and specialized
AI agents.

Cisco IQ is a suite of AI-powered applications designed to enhance the
customer experience by delivering real-time insights, assessments,
troubleshooting, learning, automation, and agent-driven guidance
throughout the entire customer lifecycle. It connects the entire customer
journey with Cisco Services, helping customers plan, deploy, manage,
secure, and optimize their IT environments. Cisco IQ provides a unified,
interactive digital experience available via SaaS, with upcoming
On-Premises and API deployment options.

Cisco AI Assistant is an intelligent, conversational AI tool integrated into
Cisco network management platforms such as the Meraki dashboard and
Cisco Catalyst Center. It enables IT teams to expedite routine tasks, gain
real-time network insights, and optimize network performance using natural
language prompts. The assistant leverages Cisco’s Deep Network Model
and global expertise to provide context-aware insights, automate routine
workflows, and accelerate troubleshooting with step-by-step guidance and
documentation summaries. It helps simplify network management by
delivering real-time health information, identifying root causes of issues,
and enabling automated configuration changes through conversational
commands. Cisco AI Assistant is designed to reduce manual errors,
increase efficiency, and empower IT teams to operate with greater
confidence and productivity across their networks

TTEC Digital’s Humanify Enterprise for Government (Humanify G) is a secure customer experience VOIP solution, powered by Cisco’s UCCE and UC Enterprise Software. Designed for agencies with up to 80,000 unified communications endpoints and 24,000 knowledge workers or agents, it allows you to scale as needed to meet citizen demand.
 
By applying technologies like journey orchestration, analytics, and AI/automation you can deliver efficient and intuitive constituent services while reducing overall contact center costs.
 
Key Features
 
Experience Cloud integrates with Humanify Enterprise Workforce Optimization SaaS (WFOaaS Quality Assurance / Call Recording / Desktop Screen Recording, Speech Analytics, and Post Call IVR surveys, powered by Verint) to enable departments and agencies to capture citizen and stakeholder feedback after interactions with contact center agents, and then utilize that input to drive coaching and feedback. TTEC Humanify Enterprise - Government platform users can now obtain the unique value of these solutions working together to drive improvements in citizen and stakeholder service.

serviceIdentification.serviceDescription:
DigiCert ONE is a unified digital trust platform that
delivers certificate lifecycle management, code signing
security, private PKI, and centralized access
governance for enterprise and government customers.
The platform is offered as a SaaS-based suite of four
integrated services:
DigiCert® Trust Lifecycle Manager (TLM) - CA-agnostic
certificate lifecycle management (CLM) providing discovery,
inventory, automated issuance and renewal, private CA
management, and integrations with ITSM and DevOps
toolchains across cloud, hybrid, and on-premises
environments.
DigiCert® Software Trust Manager (STM) - Code signing
and software supply chain security platform providing
centralized, policy-driven key and certificate management,
HSM-backed private key protection (FIPS 140-2 Level 3),
CI/CD pipeline integrations, multi-person approval
workflows, and tamperproof audit logging to support
compliance with EO 14028 and NIST SP 800-218.
DigiCert® Private CA - Private certificate authority platform
enabling organizations to create, manage, and operate
privately trusted root and intermediate CAs for issuing
certificates to internal users, devices, servers, and
workloads. Supports cloud-hosted, on-premises, and hybrid
deployment models with HSM-backed key protection and
post-quantum cryptography readiness.
DigiCert® Account Manager - Administrative and identity
governance layer of the DigiCert ONE platform providing
centralized user management, role-based access control
(RBAC), SSO/SAML configuration, API credential
management, organization management, and audit logging
across all DigiCert ONE services.

certifiedServices.serviceDescription:
DigiCert® Trust Lifecycle Manager (TLM) is a SaaS-based,
CA-agnostic certificate lifecycle management (CLM) and PKI
services platform built on the DigiCert ONE architecture.
TLM enables enterprise and government customers to
discover, inventory, automate, and govern digital certificates
(TLS/SSL, S/MIME, device, code signing) across cloud,
hybrid, and on-premises environments. Core capabilities
include certificate discovery and inventory, policy-based
issuance workflows, last-mile automation for servers and
devices, private CA creation and management, and
integrations with ITSM and DevOps toolchains. The platform
prevents certificate-related outages, reduces manual
operations overhead, and maintains continuous compliance
across the certificate estate.

DigiCert® Software Trust Manager (STM) is a SaaS-based
code signing and software supply chain security platform
built on the DigiCert ONE architecture. STM provides
centralized, policy-driven management of code signing keys
and certificates, with private keys protected in FIPS 140-2
Level 3 hardware security modules (HSMs). It integrates
natively with CI/CD pipelines (Jenkins, Azure DevOps,
GitHub Actions, Gradle) and supports remote signing via
API, CLI (SMCTL), and pre-built DevOps connectors. STM
enforces multi-person approval workflows, tracks all signing
activity in tamperproof audit logs, and helps organizations
comply with government software supply chain security
mandates including EO 14028 and NIST SP 800-218.

DigiCert® Private CA (also known as CA Manager / Private
PKI Services) is a SaaS and on-premises private certificate
authority platform within the DigiCert ONE suite. It enables
organizations to create, manage, and operate privately
trusted root and intermediate CAs for issuing certificates to
internal users, devices, servers, and workloads. Key
capabilities include HSM-backed key protection (FIPS 140-2
Level 3), support for post-quantum cryptography (ML-DSA
via Crypto4A HSMs), OCSP/CRL publishing, SCEP and
EST enrollment protocol support, and integration with
DigiCert Trust Lifecycle Manager for unified certificate
lifecycle governance. Supports deployment models including
cloud-hosted managed PKI, customer-managed on-
premises, and hybrid.

DigiCert® Account Manager is the administrative and
identity governance layer of the DigiCert ONE platform. It
provides centralized user management, role-based access
control (RBAC), single sign-on (SSO/SAML) configuration,
API token and service user credential management,
organization management, and audit logging across all
DigiCert ONE services (including Trust Lifecycle Manager,
Software Trust Manager, Private CA, and Device Trust
Manager). Account Manager is bundled with all DigiCert
ONE subscriptions and is the authoritative access control
plane for the platform. Note: Account Manager is a platform
module, not a standalone purchasable product; it is included
with each of the above service subscriptions.

certified.useCase:
AWS GovCloud (US) provides the foundational cloud
infrastructure for all DigiCert ONE services — Trust Lifecycle
Manager, Software Trust Manager, Private CA, and Account
Manager — deployed across US-East regions for

certified.justificationForUse:
AWS GovCloud is the only AWS partition designed for US
government workloads, with ITAR-compliant infrastructure,
physical access restricted to US persons, and FedRAMP
High authorization. Deployment across three availability
zones within us-gov-east-1 satisfies DigiCert ONE's high-
availability and fault-tolerance requirements for federal
customers.
certified.mitigationMeasures:
DigiCert applies application-level encryption on top of AWS
native encryption, ensuring AWS personnel cannot access
federal customer data in plaintext. Access to GovCloud
environments is restricted to vetted DigiCert personnel via
MFA-enforced IAM roles with least-privilege policies. AWS
CloudTrail logs and AWS Config are continuously monitored
for unauthorized changes.

frc-cso-pkg.agency_use_case_detail:
VirtualDojo AI CRM targets two federal markets and is intended for direct
use by federal agencies (MKT-IIP-AGU Direct Use).

Federal agencies: the platform is designed for direct agency adoption to
manage customer-relationship, procurement, and contract workflows and the
Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) involved integrated into a federal
information system under 44 U.S.C. 3506 and receiving an agency Authorization
to Operate once FedRAMP Certification is achieved.

Federal contractors: contractors performing on federal contract vehicles
(e.g., GSA Schedules, NASA SEWP VI, Army ITES) must, under DFARS 252.204-7012
and CMMC, host the CUI generated in contract performance in a cloud service
meeting the FedRAMP Moderate baseline. VirtualDojo AI CRM is built to satisfy
that requirement, maintaining federal CUI generated on behalf of those
agencies through their contractors.

Status: VirtualDojo is pursuing FedRAMP 20x Certification (Class C, Program
path) at the Moderate impact level and is in the Initial Implementation
Phase. It has not completed a FedRAMP assessment and holds no agency ATO yet;
this listing will be updated as agency adoption is confirmed.

faq.a: All customer data is stored and processed within the United States in Google Cloud under Assured Workloads (DATA_BOUNDARY_FOR_FEDRAMP_MODERATE). The primary region is us-central1 and disaster-recovery backups are replicated to us-east4; both are inside the same FedRAMP Moderate Assured Workloads enclave, so data never leaves the US boundary. All copies are encrypted with customer-managed keys (CMEK).
Data is encrypted at rest with customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) in Google Cloud KMS, and in transit with TLS 1.2+. Cryptography uses FIPS 140-validated modules.

faq.q: What compliance frameworks do you follow?
faq.a: VirtualDojo is pursuing FedRAMP 20x Certification (Class C) and a SOC 2 (Security) examination. The service is built on Google Cloud and Microsoft services that hold FedRAMP authorizations. Current status is shown on this page.

faq.q: Is VirtualDojo FedRAMP High or Moderate?
faq.a: VirtualDojo AI CRM is assessed to the FedRAMP Moderate baseline via FedRAMP 20x Certification Class C, which matches the Controlled Unclassified Information the service handles. It runs inside Google Cloud's Assured Workloads FedRAMP Moderate boundary and inherits Google's Moderate infrastructure authorization. The application's own certification is in progress.
Google Cloud, Microsoft, SendGrid, Stripe, and GitHub. Each subprocessor, its purpose, the data it handles, and its location are listed in the Subprocessors section above.

Access requires multi-factor authentication and Conditional Access via Microsoft Entra ID, enforces role-based access control and least privilege, and is continuously monitored by the automated KSI validator.

faq.q: How do you handle security incidents?
faq.a: VirtualDojo maintains documented incident-response procedures with continuous monitoring and defined notification timelines. Suspected incidents can be reported to security@virtualdojo.com.

Service availability is measured by a Google Cloud uptime check on app.virtualdojo.com, and 46 Key Security Indicators are validated nightly in-boundary. A rolling availability percentage publishes on this page as monitoring history accrues.

faq.q: What data does the service handle?
faq.a: The service handles Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) including government contract data, customer PII, proposal documents, and pricing data, at the FedRAMP Moderate impact level.

faq.q: How can a federal agency access the full certification package?
faq.a: The Certification Package (Certification Package Overview, Security Decision Record, and Ongoing Certification Reports) is available through authenticated self-service access at trust.virtualdojo.com/request-access federal (.gov/.mil) requesters are granted access automatically; other requests are reviewed under NDA. After signing in, human-readable report pages and the machine-readable JSON are both available under /reports.

continuous_progress.statement: VirtualDojo is pursuing FedRAMP 20x Certification Class C for VirtualDojo AI CRM by the Program path. Progress below is measured against dated milestones and refreshed at least quarterly. Milestones that are not yet met say so.

goals.title: Continuous, automated validation of all Key Security Indicators
goals.detail: Every applicable Key Security Indicator is verified and validated by an automated, scheduled process with retained per-day evidence, meeting the Class C floor of at least two automated methods per indicator.

goals.title: Complete, machine-readable certification data published openly
goals.detail: Certification data is published as valid JSON against the FedRAMP schemas, retrievable without negotiation, and kept current.

goals.title: Independent assessment and Program certification
goals.detail: An independent assessment by a FedRAMP Recognized assessment service, followed by application for Certification.

milestones.title: Scheduled, non-interactive KSI validation operating daily
milestones.detail: Cloud Scheduler triggers a Cloud Run job daily at 04:00 UTC under a dedicated service account. The first scheduled firing was 2026-07-04 at 04:00 UTC; per-indicator results are retained for every day since. The job was created on 2026-07-03 and the runs that day were started by hand, so 2026-07-03 is reported as manual and is not counted as persistent validation.

milestones.title: Two or more automated validation methods for every indicator
milestones.detail: Class C requires at least two automated methods per indicator (FRC-CSX-VVK). Method independence and outcome-based validation evidence are being strengthened indicator by indicator.

measured.source: latest validation run (indicators with 2+ PASSING automated methods)

milestones.title: Six months of continuous validation history
milestones.detail: FRC-CSX-MOT requires six months of historical metrics from persistent validation at Class C. The mechanism is in place and accumulating; the six-month point is reached on 2027-01-03.

milestones.title: Public certification data published and schema-valid
milestones.detail: Certification data is published at https://trust.virtualdojo.com and validated against the FedRAMP Certification Package Overview schema.

milestones.title: FedRAMP Marketplace listing obtained
milestones.detail: Marketplace Provider Listing Request submitted to FedRAMP. Listing is a prerequisite to applying for Certification (FRC-APP-MLF).

milestones.title: Independent assessment scheduled
milestones.detail: Engagement with a FedRAMP Recognized independent assessment service. The assessment must be less than three months old at application (FRC-APP-FIA).

milestones.title: Application for FedRAMP Certification submitted
milestones.detail: Submitted once the Marketplace listing is in place and the independent assessment is complete and fresh.

scheduled.meaning: The scheduled validation job ran unattended on this date at its documented 04:00 UTC cycle and produced per-indicator results. This is the only class that counts as persistent validation.

manual.meaning: Validation ran on this date but was started by hand, outside the scheduled cycle. Not counted as persistent validation.

reconstructed.meaning: Status derived after the fact from retained audit evidence. Not the output of validation performed on this date.

certification_data_access.agency_inventory:
CDS-TRC-AAI. The inventory of federal agency users and systems holding
access to FedRAMP Certification Data is the membership of the Microsoft
Entra group VDJ-TrustCenter-Agencies, which is the group the self-service
provisioning flow grants into. The history of that access is retained
separately from current membership: every grant, denial and access event
is written to Cloud Logging with the principal, the resource and the
outcome, on buckets whose 400-day retention is locked, so a record
survives the removal of a user from the group.

FedRAMP may obtain either by emailing security@virtualdojo.com. The
current inventory is supplied as a group membership export and the
history as the corresponding access records for the requested period,
within 5 business days of the request.
certification_data_access.historical_snapshots:
CDS-CSO-HAD. Snapshots of FedRAMP Certification Data are aligned to
Ongoing Certification Reports and retained for the duration of the
certification. Each Ongoing Certification Report is published with the
Certification Package as it stood at that report, reachable through the
authenticated trust center under /reports and programmatically under
/api/certification-package, and the underlying validation run for each
report is retained in the append-only evidence bucket.

All necessary parties obtain a snapshot by selecting the corresponding
report in the trust center, or by requesting a specific period from
security@virtualdojo.com.

No Ongoing Certification Report has been issued yet: this offering is not
yet certified and its first report is due 2026-10-02. Per the note on
CDS-CSO-HAD, snapshots are not reconstructed for periods before the first
Ongoing Certification Report, so none is outstanding. The retention
mechanism above is in place ahead of that first report.

trustCenter.repositoryDescription:
Request access self-service at https://trust.virtualdojo.com/request-access.
Federal agency and FedRAMP personnel with a .gov or .mil email are granted
access automatically (just-in-time) accept the emailed invitation, then
sign in with your work email. Customers and prospective customers are
reviewed by the security team (a non-disclosure or customer agreement must
be on file; typically within 2 business days). Signed-in users can view
validation reports and the certification package at

trustCenter.accessRequestInstructions:
The trust center landing page at https://trust.virtualdojo.com, the public
FedRAMP certification data feed, and the Secure Configuration Guide are
available to anyone with no account and no request required.

Access to the full Certification Package (Certification Package Overview,
Security Decision Record, and Ongoing Certification Reports) and to the
detailed validation reports under https://trust.virtualdojo.com/reports is
granted on request at https://trust.virtualdojo.com/request-access.
Requesters with a .gov or .mil email address are provisioned automatically
(just in time): submit the address, then accept the emailed invitation and
sign in with that work email. Requests from all other addresses are
reviewed by the VirtualDojo security team and require a non-disclosure or
customer agreement on file, typically completed within 2 business days.

Every document is available in both human-readable and machine-readable
form, with the JSON linked alongside each report and also reachable through
the authenticated API under /api/. For automated or programmatic
integrations, contact security@virtualdojo.com to be issued machine
credentials.

Access to FedRAMP Certification Data is logged. Each record identifies the
requesting principal, the resource reached and the outcome, and the records
are retained for 400 days, which exceeds the six months CDS-TRC-ACL
requires. An agency, assessor or customer may request a summary of its own
access by emailing security@virtualdojo.com from an address already
provisioned for trust center access; the summary covers that party's own
activity only and is supplied within 5 business days.
